definition_zh: 有机的；与生物体有关的；含碳骨架的（化学）；不用化肥农药的（农业）；自然生长而成的
definition_en: relating to living things or to carbon-based compounds, and by extension grown without synthetic chemicals or developed naturally as a whole
core_image: 一棵植物从土壤里长出来，根、茎、叶彼此相连，整株像一件长成的器官而不是拼装的零件
scene: 这些蔬菜不用合成农药和可溶性化肥，摊位上挂着醒目的标签。Organic vegetables are grown without synthetic pesticides or soluble fertilizers.
sceneCN: 这里 organic 指「有机的（不用化肥农药的）」（第 3 个义项：农业上指以有机方式种植）；蔬菜不用合成农药与可溶化肥。图中可辨识物件：植物、土壤、根茎叶的连通、无化学瓶罐；对应第 1 个义项。

有机的；生物体的；含碳的；有机耕作的；自然演成的

senses.title: Of living things
senses.definition: relating to living organisms or to the structures they build
senses.definitionCN: 与活生物或其构成的构造相关
senses.example: Soil organic matter feeds the whole food web.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤有机物养活了整个食物网。
senses.why: Greek organon named a tool, and a body's tools are its organs; 'organic' therefore starts as 'having organs', that is, belonging to a living body.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 organon 指工具，而身体的工具就是器官；因此 organic 起初意为「有器官的」，即属于活体。

senses.title: Carbon-based chemistry
senses.titleCN: 有机化学义：含碳骨架的化合物
senses.definition: describing compounds built on carbon skeletons, the chemistry once thought to require life
senses.definitionCN: 描述以碳骨架为基础的化合物，这一化学领域曾被以为只能由生命产生
senses.example: Methane is the simplest organic compound.
senses.exampleCN: 甲烷是最简单的有机化合物。
senses.why: because such compounds were first obtained only from living things, the word was carried over to the whole class even after they were synthesized in the lab.
senses.whyCN: 由于这类化合物最初只能从生物得到，即使后来能在实验室合成，这个词仍被沿用到整类物质上。

senses.title: Grown without synthetics
senses.titleCN: 农业义：不用化肥农药的
senses.definition: describing food grown without synthetic pesticides or soluble mineral fertilizers
senses.definitionCN: 描述不用合成农药或可溶矿物肥料的种植方式
senses.example: Organic apples cost more because the orchard yields less.
senses.exampleCN: 有机苹果更贵，因为果园产量更低。
senses.why: the farming sense borrows the idea of a whole living system, treating the soil as something to be fed rather than dosed.
senses.whyCN: 农业义借用「活着的整体系统」这一观念，把土壤当作需要喂养的东西，而不是投药的对象。

senses.title: Grown as a whole, not assembled
senses.titleCN: 演化义：自然生长、整体关联的
senses.definition: describing something that develops naturally as an interconnected whole rather than being assembled from parts
senses.definitionCN: 描述作为相互关联的整体自然发展，而非由零件拼装
senses.example: The firm's growth was organic, not the result of acquisitions.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司的增长是自然生长，而非并购的结果。
senses.why: since the body grows from within, 'organic' also means growth by inner development rather than by outside assembly, and business borrowed that.
senses.whyCN: 由于身体是从内部长成的，organic 也指由内在发展而非外部拼装的成长，商业领域借用了这一层。

senses.title: Of the organs in medicine
senses.definition: describing disease that has a structural change in an organ rather than a purely functional one
senses.definitionCN: 描述器官有结构改变、而非纯功能性的疾病
senses.example: The scan ruled out organic disease of the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描排除了胃的器质性病变。
senses.why: medicine must separate damage to an organ from symptoms without a lesion, so 'organic' marks the structural case.
senses.whyCN: 医学必须把器官的结构损伤与无病灶的症状分开，因此 organic 标记结构性的那一类。

senses.title: Parts that belong together
senses.titleCN: 结构义：组织上相互关联的
senses.definition: describing a structure whose parts are interdependent, like the organs of a body
senses.definitionCN: 描述各部分相互依赖的结构，如同身体的器官
senses.example: The report describes an organic link between the two agencies.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把两个机构之间的关系描述为有机联系。
senses.why: if organs serve one body, then any set of parts serving one end can be called organic.
senses.whyCN: 如果各器官服务于同一个身体，那么任何共赴一目的的一组部件都可以叫 organic。

senses.title: Foundational law and acts
senses.titleCN: 根本性义：作为根本法规的
senses.definition: describing a basic constitutional document or act, as in organic law
senses.definitionCN: 描述根本性的宪制文件或法令，如「组织法」
senses.example: The status of the territory is set by an organic act.
senses.exampleCN: 该领地的地位由一部组织法规定。
senses.why: a body needs a skeleton, so a state's founding instrument is called organic: it is what the rest is built onto.
senses.whyCN: 身体需要骨骼，因此国家的立国文件被称为「有机的」：其余一切都建在它之上。

senses.title: Whole food, whole system
senses.titleCN: 食品义：作为整体未被拆解的
senses.definition: describing food or a system treated as an intact whole rather than as isolated components
senses.definitionCN: 描述被当作完整整体、而非孤立成分处理的食品或系统
senses.example: The shop sells organics alongside conventional produce.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店把有机产品与常规农产品并排出售。
senses.why: the market turned the adjective into a noun, so 'organics' now names the goods themselves.
senses.whyCN: 市场把这个形容词变成名词，因此 organics 现在指商品本身。

intro.en: Organic comes from Greek organon 'tool, instrument', through Latin organum and the medieval adjective organicus. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: organic 出自希腊 organon「工具、器具」，经拉丁 organum 与中世纪形容词 organicus 而来。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: organon named a tool or instrument, and in philosophy a means of doing something. From it comes the sense of a body part that does work.
items.cn: organon 指工具或器具，也指哲学上达成某目的的手段。由它引申出「做工作的身体部件」这一义。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument and, in later use, a musical instrument; the body-part sense developed in anatomy.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum 指器具，后亦指乐器；身体部件的义项在解剖学中发展起来。

items.en: Medieval Latin organicus meant 'of an organ' or 'having organs'; English took the adjective in this anatomical sense first.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 organicus 意为「器官的」或「有器官的」；英语先在这个解剖学意义上使用该形容词。

items.en: Around 1800 chemists divided compounds into organic, from living things, and inorganic; urea's laboratory synthesis in 1828 weakened the boundary but the name stayed.
items.cn: 约 1800 年，化学家把化合物分为来自生物的 organic 与 inorganic；1828 年尿素在实验室被合成，动摇了这条界线，但名称保留。

items.en: The twentieth century applied the word to farming that avoids synthetic inputs, treating soil as a living system.
items.cn: 20 世纪把这个词用于避免合成投入物的耕作方式，把土壤当作活系统。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): organon's pre-Greek origin is not established, so any Indo-European form behind it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：organon 在希腊语之前的来源并无定论，其背后的任何印欧形式都是重构，而非有记录的实际词。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek stem that name different things; group two holds words often used where organic could be chosen.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊词干、但指不同事物的词；第二组是常与 organic 互换使用的词。

entries.definition: A part of a body or an organisation, not a quality; organic is the adjective describing such a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体或机构的部件，不是性质；organic 是描述这类整体的形容词。

entries.definition: A complete living being; it shares organon but names an entity, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 指完整的生物体；共享 organon，但命名实体而非性质。

entries.definition: A structured group of people, from the same stem via 'organize'. It names an institution, not a growing whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指有结构的人群，由同一词干经 organize 而来；命名机构，不是生长的整体。

entries.definition: Not built on carbon and not from life; it is the direct opposite in chemistry and farming.
entries.definitionCN: 不以碳为基础、非来自生命；在化学与农业中与 organic 直接相对。

entries.definition: Not made or altered by humans; organic in farming also implies natural methods, but natural says nothing about certification.
entries.definitionCN: 非人力制造或改动的；农业中的 organic 也含自然方式，但 natural 不涉及认证。

entries.definition: Relating to biology or to living processes; it names the science, while organic names a property of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物学或生命过程相关；命名学科，而 organic 命名物质属性。

entries.definition: Good for health or morally sound; organic food is often called wholesome, but the words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 有益健康或品德端正；有机食品常被称 wholesome，但两词回答不同问题。

entries.definition: Arranged by an outside plan; organic growth is the opposite of planned assembly.
entries.definitionCN: 按外部方案安排；organic growth 恰与计划拼装相反。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek organon 'tool': a body's tools are its organs, so organic first means 'having organs'.
normal.cn: 希腊 organon「工具」：身体的工具就是器官，所以 organic 起初意为「有器官的」。

normal.en: The family runs organ, organism, organization, organic, organically, inorganic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organ、organism、organization、organic、organically、inorganic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: organic matter, organic compound, organic farming, organic growth, organic chemistry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：有机物、有机化合物、有机农业、自然增长、有机化学。

normal.en: Chemistry pairs it with inorganic; farming pairs it with conventional.
normal.cn: 化学中与 inorganic 相对；农业中与常规耕作相对。

normal.en: The business sense is 'grown from within', the opposite of bought through acquisitions.
normal.cn: 商业义是「从内部长成」，与靠并购得来相反。

abstract.en: Picture a plant whose root, stem and leaf all serve one life.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物，根、茎、叶都服务于同一条生命。

abstract.en: Picture a city that grew along its roads instead of being stamped out at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市沿道路长出来，而不是一次压印成形。

abstract.en: Picture a table whose legs are not attached but grown from the same wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，桌腿不是装上去的，而是与桌面同一块木料长出来的。

examples.en: Organic matter in the soil holds water between grains.
examples.cn: 土壤中的有机物在颗粒之间持水。

examples.en: Organic chemistry began with compounds isolated from plants and animals.
examples.cn: 有机化学始于从动植物中分离出的化合物。

examples.en: The company preferred organic growth to borrowing for acquisitions.
examples.cn: 公司更愿自然增长，而不是借钱并购。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「有器官（organ）的」——凡活物长成的、含碳的、不用化肥的 → 有机的

root: 希腊 organon「工具、器具」→ 拉丁 organum → 中世纪拉丁 organicus「有器官的」→ 英语 organic；19 世纪扩展为化学义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: a body's parts all serve one life; that image is read as living matter, as carbon chemistry, as chemical-free farming, as growth from within, as structural disease, as interdependence, as a founding law, and as goods sold under that label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：身体的各部分都服务于同一条生命；这一意象依次被读成生命物质、碳化学、无合成投入的耕作、由内生长、器质性疾病、相互依赖、立国根本法，以及以此标签出售的商品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: root, stem and leaf all serving one living whole, with nothing bolted on.
core.cn: 核心意象：根、茎、叶都服务于同一个活的整体，没有一件是外装的。

branches.en: LIVING MATTER: the oldest sense, matter that belongs to a body.
branches.cn: 生命物质：最古老的义项，属于身体的物质。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: the carbon class, named when such compounds came only from life.
branches.cn: 化学：碳化合物这一类，命名时它们只来自生命。

branches.en: FARMING AND GOODS: soil fed as a living system, and produce sold as organics.
branches.cn: 农业与商品：把土壤当活系统来养，以及作为 organic 产品出售。

branches.en: GROWTH: development from within, borrowed by business for unplanned expansion.
branches.cn: 生长：由内发展，商业借指非计划性扩张。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: organ damage in medicine, interdependent parts, and a state's founding law.
branches.cn: 结构：医学上的器官损伤、相互依赖的部件，以及国家的立国根本法。

intro.en: Organic is Greek organon plus the Latin adjectival ending -icus, kept in English as -ic; the family also uses -ism and -ize.
intro.cn: organic 是希腊 organon 加拉丁形容词词尾 -icus，在英语中保留为 -ic；词族还用 -ism 与 -ize。

latinIntro.en: Latin organum is a borrowed Greek word, and medieval organicus is a Latin formation on it; both are real Latin, though the root is Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 organum 是借自希腊语的词，中世纪 organicus 是在其上形成的拉丁词；二者都是真实的拉丁语，但词根属希腊语。

senses.title: An Individual Living Thing
senses.definition: a single living thing, such as an animal, plant or bacterium
senses.definitionCN: 单个活物，如动物、植物或细菌
senses.example: A single organism can contain more cells than there are people in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 一个生物体内的细胞数可能超过这座城市的人口。
senses.why: Greek organon meant 'tool, instrument'. An organism is a body whose parts work as instruments for the whole, which is why the word stresses organized cooperation rather than mere life.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 organon 意为「工具、器具」；organism 是各部件作为整体之工具而协同工作的身体，因此这个词强调有组织的协作，而不只是「活着」。

senses.title: Microscopic Life
senses.titleCN: 微生物：肉眼难见的个体
senses.definition: a microscopic living thing, especially a bacterium or fungus
senses.definitionCN: 微小的活物，尤指细菌或真菌
senses.example: The water contained several harmful organisms.
senses.exampleCN: 水中含有几种有害微生物。
senses.why: In hygiene and medicine the word usually points to things too small to see. The size is not part of the definition, but the context supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 在卫生与医学语境里，这个词通常指小到看不见的东西；大小并不属于定义，而是由语境补上的。

senses.title: A Social Whole
senses.titleCN: 有机整体：社会或组织的比喻
senses.definition: a society or organization treated as a body whose parts depend on one another
senses.definitionCN: 被看作相互依存之身体的社会或组织
senses.example: Some nineteenth-century writers called society a living organism.
senses.exampleCN: 一些十九世纪的作家把社会称为活的有机体。
senses.why: The metaphor claims that institutions are not assembled machines but growing bodies. It has been used both to justify reform and to argue that parts cannot be replaced at will.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻主张制度不是拼装的机器，而是生长出来的身体；它既被用来支持改革，也被用来论证各部分不能随意替换。

senses.title: Engineered Life
senses.titleCN: 改造过的生物：转基因个体
senses.definition: a living thing whose genetic material has been deliberately altered
senses.definitionCN: 遗传物质被人为改动的活物
senses.example: Regulations cover any genetically modified organism sold as food.
senses.exampleCN: 法规涵盖任何作为食品出售的转基因生物。
senses.why: Modern biotechnology made the word a legal category. The organism is still an individual living thing; only its genes have been edited, which is why the modifier carries the weight.
senses.whyCN: 现代生物技术把这个词变成法律类别；该生物仍是独立活物，只是基因被编辑过，因此分量落在修饰语上。

senses.title: Model Organism
senses.titleCN: 模式生物：用于研究的代表
senses.definition: a species studied in the laboratory to understand general biological processes
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室中研究、以理解一般生物过程的物种
senses.example: The fruit fly became the model organism for genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 果蝇成了遗传学的模式生物。
senses.why: Research needs a stand-in that is easy to keep and well understood. The word marks the individual, while the phrase marks its representative role.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要一个易饲养、已被充分理解的替身；这个词标出的是个体，而短语标出的是它的代表角色。

senses.title: An Ecological Unit
senses.titleCN: 生态个体：生态学中的计数单位
senses.definition: an individual counted as a unit in an ecological study
senses.definitionCN: 生态研究中作为一个单位来计数的个体
senses.example: The survey counted every organism larger than a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 该调查统计了每一个大于一毫米的生物个体。
senses.why: Ecology counts individuals to estimate populations. Here the word is almost a unit of measurement, defined by the size cut-off the researcher chooses.
senses.whyCN: 生态学通过数个体来估计种群；此时这个词几乎是一个计量单位，其边界由研究者选定的尺寸下限决定。

senses.title: An Organized Whole
senses.titleCN: 有机整体：哲学意义上的整体
senses.definition: a whole whose parts are mutually dependent and cannot be understood alone
senses.definitionCN: 各部分相互依赖、不能孤立理解的整体
senses.example: For the philosopher, the mind is an organism, not a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 在这位哲学家看来，心灵是有机整体，而不是机器。
senses.why: Philosophy uses the word against mechanism. If parts only make sense in the whole, explanation must begin with the whole, not with the smallest piece.
senses.whyCN: 哲学用这个词来反对机械论：如果部件只有在整体中才有意义，解释就必须从整体开始，而不是从最小零件开始。

senses.title: A Working Body
senses.titleCN: 运作中的组织体：机构如身体
senses.definition: an organization understood through the cooperation of its parts
senses.definitionCN: 通过各部分协作来理解的机构
senses.example: The department behaves like an organism with its own metabolism.
senses.exampleCN: 这个部门像一个有自己的代谢方式的有机体那样运作。
senses.why: Management writing borrows the biological image to talk about flow, feedback and adaptation. The claim is that removing one part changes the health of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 管理写作借生物学意象来谈流动、反馈与适应；其主张是：拿掉一个部件会改变其余部分的健康。

intro.en: Organism is a modern formation on Greek organon 'tool, instrument, organ', from ergon 'work'. It was coined in the nineteenth century; the exact coiner and first date are uncertain.
intro.cn: organism 是建立在希腊 organon「工具、器具、器官」之上的近代构词，而 organon 出自 ergon「工作」。该词于十九世纪被造出；确切的造词者与首见年代不确定。

items.en: Ergon meant 'work, deed'. Its Indo-European root also gives English work and the Greek adjective energetikos, source of energy.
items.cn: ergon 意为「工作、行动」，其印欧词根也给出英语 work，以及希腊形容词 energetikos——energy 的来源。

items.en: Organon meant 'a tool or instrument', and by extension an organ of the body, since an organ is the body's instrument for a task. Aristotle's logical works were called the Organon, the tool of reasoning.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，引申指身体器官，因为器官就是身体完成某项任务的工具。亚里士多德的逻辑著作被称为 Organon，即推理的工具。

items.en: Latin organum kept the senses of instrument and, later, musical instrument and body organ. English organ and organize descend from this line.
items.cn: 拉丁 organum 保留「器具」义，后来又指乐器与身体器官；英语 organ 与 organize 都出自这条线索。

items.en: Organism was formed in the nineteenth century to name a living body as an organized whole. The exact coiner is uncertain; the word spread with biology and with the philosophy of organized wholes.
items.cn: organism 于十九世纪被造出，用来指作为有组织整体的活体。确切的造词者不确定；该词随生物学以及「有组织整体」的哲学而传播开来。

items.en: Social thinkers soon applied organism to societies and institutions. The metaphor was attractive because it explained interdependence, but it was also criticized for making change seem like mere growth.
items.cn: 社会思想家很快把 organism 用于社会与机构。这个比喻之所以有吸引力，是因为它能解释相互依存；但它也因让变革显得只是「生长」而受到批评。

note.en: The first group separates the noun from its adjective relatives and from organization. The second holds near-synonyms that name life at different scales.
note.cn: 第一组区分该名词与其形容词亲属以及 organization；第二组是不同尺度上指称生命的近义词。

entries.definition: Means 'of living things' or 'grown without chemicals'. It describes a quality, while organism names the living individual.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「生物的」或「不用化学方式种植的」；它描述性质，而 organism 命名的是活的个体。

entries.definition: A structured group such as a company, or the act of arranging. It shares the organ root but names arrangement, not life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指公司一类有结构的人群，或安排的动作；它同出 organ 词根，但命名的是安排，而不是生命。

entries.definition: A body part with a specific function, or a musical instrument. It is the instrument that the organism as a whole uses.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指有特定功能的身体部件，或指乐器；它是整个 organism 所使用的「工具」。

entries.definition: A living being, especially an animal. It is warmer and less technical than organism.
entries.definitionCN: 活物，尤指动物；比 organism 更有温度，技术性更弱。

entries.definition: A living entity, or existence itself. It is broader and vaguer, often used where organism would sound clinical.
entries.definitionCN: 活的存在者，或存在本身；更宽泛、更模糊，在 organism 显得过于临床的地方常用它。

entries.definition: A microscopic living thing. It is narrower than organism, which covers elephants as well as bacteria.
entries.definitionCN: 微小的活物；比 organism 狭窄，因为后者同样包括大象与细菌。

entries.definition: Any kind of living thing, often used when imagining life elsewhere. It stresses kind rather than individual.
entries.definitionCN: 任何种类的活物，常用于设想别处的生命；强调种类而非个体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: organon 'tool' + -ism: a body whose organs are tools for the whole.
normal.cn: organon「工具」+ -ism：器官作为整体工具的身体。

normal.en: The family runs organ, organic, organism, organismal, organismic, organize, organization, organelle.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organ、organic、organism、organismal、organismic、organize、organization、organelle。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: living organism, model organism, single-celled organism, genetically modified organism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：生物、模式生物、单细胞生物、转基因生物。

normal.en: organism is the living thing; organization is the arranged group.
normal.cn: organism 是活的东西，organization 是安排成的群体。

normal.en: organic describes a quality; organism names the individual.
normal.cn: organic 描述性质，organism 命名个体。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where every tool has its place and every worker serves the same finished object.
abstract.cn: 想象一间作坊，每件工具都有位置，每个工人服务于同一件成品。

abstract.en: Picture a city that repairs its own roads without anyone giving the order.
abstract.cn: 想象一座自己修补道路、无需谁下命令的城市。

abstract.en: Picture a watch that grows new wheels instead of replacing them.
abstract.cn: 想象一只表会自己长出新的齿轮，而不是更换齿轮。

examples.en: No organism can survive without water for long.
examples.cn: 没有生物能在缺水的情况下长期存活。

examples.en: The pond supports thousands of microscopic organisms.
examples.cn: 这个池塘养育着数以千计的微小生物。

examples.en: The model organism is chosen because its genome is small.
examples.cn: 选择该模式生物，是因为它的基因组很小。

dict_mnemonic.text: organ（器官）+ ism（体系、状态）→ 由器官协同构成的整体 → 生物、有机体

root: 希腊 ergon「工作」→ organon「工具、器官」→ 拉丁 organum → 英语 organ → 十九世纪加 -ism 构成 organism。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all concern an organized living whole: an individual, a microbe, a society, an engineered plant or animal, a laboratory model, an ecological unit, a philosophical whole and a working institution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都涉及有组织的活的整体：个体、微生物、社会、被改造的动植物、实验室模型、生态单位、哲学整体与运作中的机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many organs working as one body, each part serving the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多器官作为一个身体协同工作，每个部件都为整体服务。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL UNIT: from a whale to a bacterium, one living thing counted as one.
branches.cn: 个体单位：从鲸到细菌，一个活物算作一个。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE MAJORITY: hygiene and medicine use the word for life too small to see.
branches.cn: 看不见的多数：卫生与医学用这个词指小到看不见的生命。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL METAPHOR: societies and departments are described as bodies whose parts depend on each other.
branches.cn: 社会比喻：社会与部门被描述为部件相互依存的身体。

branches.en: LIFE UNDER DESIGN: engineered organisms and model organisms exist because humans chose and altered them.
branches.cn: 被设计过的生命：转基因生物与模式生物之所以存在，是因为人选择并改动了它们。

branches.en: THE PHILOSOPHICAL WHOLE: against mechanism, the whole explains the parts rather than the reverse.
branches.cn: 哲学整体：与机械论相对，整体解释部件，而不是反过来。

intro.en: Organism is a Greek-derived root with the English suffix -ism: an instrument-root, a suffix of system or state, and later a biological noun.
intro.cn: organism 是希腊来源的词根加英语后缀 -ism：表示器具的词根、表示体系或状态的后缀，后来成为生物学名词。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon reached Latin as organum and produced organ, organic, organism, organize, organization and organelle. The root ergon also underlies energy.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 以拉丁 organum 进入拉丁语，衍生 organ、organic、organism、organize、organization、organelle；词根 ergon 也支撑 energy。

items.example: The organism responds to light within seconds.
items.exampleCN: 该生物在数秒内就对光作出反应。

items.meaning: of living things; grown without chemicals
items.meaningCN: 生物的；不用化学方式种植的
items.example: Organic matter in the soil feeds the crop.
items.exampleCN: 土壤中的有机物滋养作物。

items.meaning: at the level of the individual organism
items.example: Organismal responses differ from cellular ones.
items.exampleCN: 个体层面的反应不同于细胞层面的反应。

items.meaning: treating the whole as an organized body
items.example: Organismic biology studies wholes, not only parts.
items.exampleCN: 有机体生物学研究整体，而不只是部件。

items.meaning: a body part with a task
items.meaningCN: 承担某项任务的身体部件
items.example: The liver is the largest internal organ.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏是最大的内部器官。

items.meaning: a small structure inside a cell
to arrange parts into a working whole
items.meaningCN: 把部件安排成可运作的整体
items.example: She organized the files by year.

items.meaning: an arranged group or the act of arranging
items.meaningCN: 安排成的群体或安排的行为

definition_zh: 组织；机构；企业；编排；整理；组织结构
definition_en: a group of people with a particular purpose and structure, or the act of arranging things into an ordered system
core_image: 一张桌上摊开的机构图，方框之间用直线连成层级，没有一处悬空
scene: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处。The international organization keeps offices in three countries.
sceneCN: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处；句中的 organization 指「为特定目的而设立的机构」（第 2 个义项：机构、团体）。图中可辨识物件：机构图、办事处门牌、文件夹、地球仪；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A group with a purpose and a structure
senses.definition: a group of people working together with defined roles towards a shared aim
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目标而按既定角色协作的一群人
senses.example: Every organization needs someone to keep the records.
senses.exampleCN: 每个组织都需要有人保管记录。
senses.why: The word comes from the Greek word for a tool, and an organization is a group arranged like an instrument for a purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自希腊语中表示「工具」的词，组织就是为某个目的像器具一样被安排起来的一群人。

senses.title: An institution or body
senses.definition: an established body such as a charity, a union, a hospital or an international agency
senses.definitionCN: 已设立的机构，如慈善团体、工会、医院或国际机构
senses.example: The international organization keeps offices in three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处。
senses.why: Once a group acquires a name, rules and premises, it is spoken of as an institution rather than a gathering.
senses.whyCN: 当一群人有了名称、规则与办公场所，人们就说它是机构，而不只是一次聚会。

senses.title: A company treated as a body
senses.definition: a business viewed as a structured body of departments, staff and procedures
senses.definitionCN: 被视为由部门、人员与流程构成的企业
senses.example: The organization employs four hundred people across six sites.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业在六个地点雇了四百人。
senses.why: Calling a firm an organization shifts attention from its trade to its internal arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 把企业称作 organization，注意力就从它的买卖转到它的内部安排。

senses.title: The act of arranging something
senses.definition: the act of putting parts, events or tasks into a workable order
senses.definitionCN: 把各部分、活动或任务排成可运作次序的动作
senses.example: The organization of the festival took six months.
senses.exampleCN: 节庆的组织工作花了六个月。
senses.why: Before the word meant a body, it meant the act of giving parts an order, and that act still carries the name.
senses.whyCN: 在指团体之前，这个词指「给各部分定次序」的动作，这个动作至今仍用这个名称。

senses.title: The structure itself
senses.definition: the pattern of departments, ranks and reporting lines inside a body
senses.definitionCN: 机构内部部门、层级与汇报线的格局
senses.example: The new director redrew the organization within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 新主管在一年内重画了组织结构。
senses.why: If organizing is giving order, the resulting order is also called by the same name.
senses.whyCN: 如果组织是赋予次序，那么产生的次序也用同一个名称。

senses.title: The quality of being orderly
senses.definition: the quality of doing things in an ordered, planned way
senses.definitionCN: 以有序、有计划的方式做事的性质
senses.example: Her organization kept the whole project on schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 她的条理性让整个项目按计划推进。
senses.why: A person can possess the same order that a body has, so the noun also names a personal capacity.
senses.whyCN: 一个人也可以拥有团体那样的秩序，因此这个名词也指个人能力。

senses.title: The arrangement of living tissue
senses.definition: the structured arrangement of cells and tissues in a living body
senses.definitionCN: 活体中细胞与组织的结构安排
senses.example: The microscope revealed the organization of the leaf tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜显示出叶片组织的构造。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the word for the ordered arrangement of parts in a living thing, from the same tool image.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用这个词，指活体中各部分有序的安排，仍沿用「器具」的意象。

senses.title: An international body
senses.definition: a body set up by states or by agreement across borders to handle shared matters
senses.definitionCN: 由国家设立或跨国协议建立、处理共同事务的机构
senses.example: The organization was founded to coordinate relief after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国际组织是为协调战后救济而设立的。
senses.why: States needed permanent instruments for shared work, and the tool sense of the root fits that role exactly.
senses.whyCN: 各国需要为共同事务设立常设工具，词根的「器具」义正好契合这一角色。

intro.en: Organization comes from organize, built on Latin organum 'instrument', from Greek organon 'tool'. It first named the act of arranging and later the body so arranged. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: organization 来自 organize，其基础是拉丁 organum「器具」，再溯至希腊 organon「工具」。它先指安排的动作，后指被安排成的团体。年代均为约数。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument', and Greek philosophy used it for an instrument of reasoning as well as a physical tool.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，希腊哲学既用它指推理的工具，也指实物器具。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument, and it also named a musical instrument and, later, a bodily organ.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum 指器具，也用来指乐器，后来又指身体器官。

items.en: The verb organize meant to give parts an order so that they work together, like fitting tools to a task.
items.cn: 动词 organize 意为给各部分定次序使它们协同运作，像把工具配到一项任务上。

items.en: In English organization first named the act of arranging; by the eighteenth century it named the body that results.
items.cn: 在英语中，organization 先指安排的动作；到十八世纪才指由此形成的团体。

items.en: Industrial and international bodies made the word the standard term for any structured group, from charities to agencies.
items.cn: 工业与国际机构使这个词成为任何有结构团体的标准称呼，从慈善团体到政府机构。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same organ root; group two holds words for structured groups.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「器具」词根的各种形式；第二组是表示有结构团体的词。

entries.definition: To arrange things or people into order; the act behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物或人排成次序；是名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: A part of a body or a musical instrument, from the same tool word; it is not a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体器官或乐器，同出「器具」一词；不是团体。

entries.definition: An individual living being, whose parts are organized; it is a creature, not an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个活体，其各部分有组织；是生物，不是机构。

entries.definition: Relating to an organization or its structure; it describes, while organization names.
entries.definitionCN: 与组织或其结构有关的形容词；描述性质，organization 命名实体。

entries.definition: An established body or custom with social standing; it stresses endurance, not internal arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指有社会地位的既定机构或惯例；强调持久，不强调内部安排。

entries.definition: A group of people joined for a shared interest, usually voluntarily; often smaller than an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 指为共同兴趣自愿结合的一群人；通常比 organization 小。

entries.definition: Any group treated as a unit, such as a governing body; it is vaguer about structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指被当作单位处理的任何群体，如管理机构；对结构说得更含糊。

entries.definition: A business, usually a professional partnership; it cannot name a charity or an agency.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业，通常是专业合伙；不能指慈善团体或政府机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Greek for tool: a group arranged like an instrument for a purpose.
normal.cn: 希腊语意为「工具」：为某个目的像器具一样被安排起来的一群人。

normal.en: The family runs organize, organization, organizational, organizer and organism.
normal.cn: 同族词有 organize、organization、organizational、organizer 与 organism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: a non-profit organization, an international organization, the organization of work.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各义项：非营利组织、国际组织、工作的安排。

normal.en: The same root gives organ, a body part that is itself a tool.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 organ，即本身就是「工具」的身体部件。

normal.en: The word first meant the act of arranging, then the body arranged.
normal.cn: 这个词先指安排的动作，后指被安排成的团体。

abstract.en: Picture a chart of boxes joined by straight lines, none of them floating.
abstract.cn: 想象一张方框图表，方框之间用直线相连，没有一个悬空。

abstract.en: Picture a toolbox where every tool hangs in its own marked place.
abstract.cn: 想象一只工具箱，每件工具都挂在标好的位置上。

abstract.en: Picture a choir that breathes together without anyone shouting.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团，没人喊叫却一起换气。

examples.en: The organization trains volunteers to teach reading.
examples.cn: 这个组织培训志愿者教阅读。

examples.en: Poor organization wasted half the budget.
examples.cn: 糟糕的统筹浪费了一半预算。

examples.en: She is known for her organization and calm under pressure.
examples.cn: 她以有条理和临压不乱而出名。

root: 拉丁 organum「器具」，来自希腊 organon「工具」；动词 organize 指给各部分定次序，organization 由「安排的动作」引申为「被安排成的团体与结构」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one instrument: the purposeful group, the institution, the company as a body, the act of arranging, the structure, the personal orderliness, the living tissue, and the international body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一件「器具」：有目的的团体、机构、作为组织看待的企业、安排的动作、组织结构、个人的条理性、活体组织，以及国际机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an instrument whose parts fit together so that it can do one job.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件器具，各部件互相咬合，从而能完成一项工作。

branches.en: GROUP AS TOOL: a purpose-driven group and a company seen as a body are the same instrument at different legal sizes.
branches.cn: 作为工具的群体：为目的一组人与被视为身体的企业，是同一器具的不同法律规模。

branches.en: LASTING BODY: a charity and an international agency are institutions built to keep working.
branches.cn: 持久的身体：慈善团体与国际机构都是为持续运作而建的机构。

branches.en: FITTING TOGETHER: before there is a body there is the act of giving parts an order.
branches.cn: 装配：在团体存在之前，先有给各部分定次序的动作。

branches.en: THE ORDER ITSELF: the pattern of departments and reporting lines is the result of arranging.
branches.cn: 次序本身：部门与汇报线的格局，是安排的结果。

branches.en: NATURAL ORDER: a tidy person and living tissue both show parts kept in working order.
branches.cn: 自然秩序：有条理的人与活体组织，都显示各部分保持运作秩序。

intro.en: Organization is a Greek tool word plus a Latin action suffix, a common pattern in academic English.
intro.cn: organization 是希腊语「工具」词加拉丁动作后缀，是学术英语中常见的模式。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon passed into Latin as organum, giving organ, organize, organization and organism.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 进入拉丁作 organum，给出 organ、organize、organization 与 organism。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘配到任务上的工具。

scene: 毕业典礼前一天的礼堂里，长桌上堆着没拆的纸箱，几个人来回比对清单，把椅子一排排摆好。They spent the afternoon organizing the chairs for the ceremony.
sceneCN: 这里的 organizing 是「组织、筹备」（第 1 个义项：筹划并安排一项活动）；句意为他们花了一下午为典礼摆放椅子。图中可辨识物件：纸箱、清单、成排的椅子。

pos.zh: 组织；筹备；整理；编成团体；使有条理

derivatives.zh: 由 organize 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「组织；机构」
由 organize 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「组织者」
由 organization 加 -al 构成，义为「组织上的；机构的」

senses.title: To plan and arrange an activity or event
senses.definition: to make all the preparations needed for an activity or event, deciding who does what and when
senses.definitionCN: 为一项活动或事件做好全部准备，把谁做什么、何时做都安排妥当
senses.example: They spent the afternoon organizing the chairs for the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他们花了一下午为典礼摆放椅子。
senses.why: The Greek source organon meant a tool, and the verb came to mean fitting parts together so that a whole can work, which is exactly what planning an event does.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源头 organon 意为工具，这个动词后来指把各部分装配合用，使整体能够运转，而筹备一场活动做的正是这件事。

senses.title: To put things into a clear order
senses.definition: to arrange objects, papers or data so that they are easy to find and use
senses.definitionCN: 把物品、文件或资料排放妥当，使人容易查找和使用
senses.example: She organized her notes into three folders before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前她把笔记整理进三个文件夹。
senses.why: If a tool is a set of parts that fit, then a drawer or a folder can also be made to fit, so the same verb moves from machines to shelves and files.
senses.whyCN: 既然工具是一组彼此契合的部件，抽屉和文件夹也能被安排得彼此契合，于是同一个动词从机器走到了货架和文件。

senses.title: To form people into a group or union
senses.definition: to bring people together into a body with a shared purpose, such as a union or a team
senses.definitionCN: 把人们聚集起来，组成一个有共同目标的团体，如工会或队伍
senses.example: The workers organized a union in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们在春天组织成立了一个工会。
senses.why: People, like parts, can be brought into a working arrangement, and when they act as one body the verb names the forming of that body.
senses.whyCN: 人和零件一样可以被装进一个能运转的安排里，当他们作为一个整体行动时，这个动词指的就是这个整体的形成。

senses.title: To arrange parts into a coherent whole
senses.definition: to give separate pieces of something, such as an essay or a plan, a logical and clear structure
senses.definitionCN: 给文章、方案等分散的部分安排出合乎逻辑而清晰的结构
senses.example: The report was poorly organized, so the main point was hard to find.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告编排得很乱，主旨很难找到。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is an instrument whose parts work together, and writing is organized when each paragraph has a job in the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根最老的意思是各部件协同工作的器具，而文章之所以「有条理」，正是因为每段都在整体里担着一份职责。

intro.en: Organize came through medieval Latin from the Greek word for a tool; the tool image is the reason the verb can mean arranging parts, forming groups and giving a text a structure.
intro.cn: organize 经中世纪拉丁语上溯到希腊语中表示「工具」的词；正因为有这件工具的画面，这个动词才能表示装配部件、组成团体与安排文章结构。

items.en: Organon meant a tool or instrument, especially one made of parts that work together for a task.
items.cn: organon 意为工具、器具，尤指由若干协同工作的部件构成、用于某项任务的器具。

items.en: Latin took the word as organum, an instrument or a bodily organ, and also used it for a musical instrument.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该词作 organum，指器具或身体器官，也用来指乐器。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed organizare, to organize or to give something its organs and parts, often used of the body and of a body of people.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语造出 organizare，意为组织、赋予某物器官与部件，常用于身体，也用于一群人构成的团体。

items.en: French took the verb as organiser, meaning to arrange or to set up, and English borrowed it in the same practical sense.
items.cn: 法语把该动词作 organiser，意为安排、设立，英语借入时也带着同样实用的意味。

items.en: Modern English keeps organize for events, for shelves and files, for unions and teams, and for the structure of writing or plans.
items.cn: 现代英语让 organize 兼指活动筹备、货架与文件的整理、工会与队伍的组织，以及文章或方案的结构安排。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Greek and Latin stem for tool and organ; the near-meaning group collects verbs for putting things into order.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在希腊语与拉丁语「工具、器官」词干上的词；近义组收表示「把事物安排有序」的动词。

entries.definition: A part of the body with a special job, or a large musical instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 身体中担负特定功能的部位，或大型乐器。

entries.definition: Relating to living things, or grown without artificial chemicals.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物有关的，或不用人工化学物质种植的。

entries.definition: The act of arranging, or a group that has been arranged.
entries.definitionCN: 安排的行为，或被组织起来的团体。

entries.definition: A person who plans and arranges an event.
entries.definitionCN: 筹划并安排活动的人。

entries.definition: To put things in a particular order or position.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物按某种次序或位置放好。

entries.definition: To make different parts work together smoothly.
entries.definitionCN: 使不同部分顺畅地配合运作。

entries.definition: To separate things into groups by type.
entries.definitionCN: 按种类把事物分成组。

entries.definition: To put things into named categories.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物归入有名目的类别。

normalIntro.en: Organize rests on the Greek word for a tool, so its hooks keep the picture of separate parts being fitted into something that works.
normalIntro.cn: organize 建立在希腊语表示「工具」的词上，所以记忆钩子始终保留「分散的部件被装成一件能用的东西」的画面。

normal.en: The Greek word organon is a tool, and an organ in the body is a tool of that organ's own kind, which is why the family keeps the sense of parts that work.
normal.cn: 希腊语 organon 是工具，而身体里的器官正是各自那一类的工具，所以这一族词始终带着「部件在起作用」的意味。

normal.en: Organize ends in -ize, the verb ending that means to make or to put into a state, so to organize is to make something into an ordered body.
normal.cn: organize 以 -ize 收尾，这个动词词尾表示「使成为某种状态」，所以组织就是把某物变成一个有序的整体。

normal.en: Organization is organize plus -ation, the ending that names an action or its result, so the same stem gives both the act and the body.
normal.cn: organization 是 organize 加 -ation，这个后缀指行为或其结果，所以同一个词干既给出动作，也给出团体。

normal.en: Organize a meeting and organize information share one verb because both put scattered pieces into a workable order.
normal.cn: organize a meeting 与 organize information 共用一个动词，因为两者都把零散的东西排成可用的次序。

normal.en: Note the British spelling with s and the American spelling with z, just as organisation and organization differ.
normal.cn: 留意英式拼写用 s、美式拼写用 z，正如 organisation 与 organization 的差别。

abstract.en: A word that began with a tool reminds us that order is not decoration; it is what makes separate parts able to do something together.
abstract.cn: 一个从工具起步的词提醒人：秩序不是装饰，而是让分散部件能一起做成一件事的条件。

abstract.en: To organize people is to treat them as parts of one body, which is powerful and also a little dangerous.
abstract.cn: 把人组织起来，就是把他们当作一个整体的部件，这既有力量，也带一点危险。

abstract.en: Every tidy shelf and every clear paragraph is the same small victory over scatter.
abstract.cn: 每一个整齐的货架、每一段清晰的文字，都是对「散乱」的同一场小小胜利。

examples.en: They spent the afternoon organizing the chairs for the ceremony.
examples.cn: 他们花了一下午为典礼摆放椅子。

examples.en: She organized her notes into three folders.
examples.cn: 她把笔记整理进三个文件夹。

examples.en: The workers organized a union in the spring.
examples.cn: 工人们在春天组织成立了一个工会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，搁那儿整」——东西都搁在那儿，一件件整好；记住 organize 是整理、组织。

root: 来自中世纪拉丁语 organizare（组织、使成系统），再上溯拉丁语 organum（工具、器官），源头是希腊语 organon（器具）；同族词多与「器官、机构、有机关联的整体」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is parts fitted into a working whole; the senses divide by what is fitted together, an event, a set of objects, a group of people, or the pieces of a text.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是部件被装成一个能运转的整体；义项按被装配的对象分出：一场活动、一堆物品、一群人，或一篇文章的各个部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered parts sorted by size and screwed together into a machine that turns.
core.cn: 核心意象：散落的零件被按大小排好，拧成一台能转动的机器。

branches.en: a hall being made ready for a ceremony
branches.cn: 为典礼布置好的一座礼堂

branches.en: papers and boxes sorted into neat rows
branches.cn: 纸张与箱子被分成整齐的几排

branches.en: workers signing their names to a new union
branches.cn: 工人在新工会名册上签名

branches.en: an essay whose paragraphs finally fall into place
branches.cn: 段落终于各就各位的一篇文章

branches.en: the same verb for an event and a shelf
branches.cn: 同一个动词，既用于活动，也用于货架

intro.en: The word is a Greek tool-noun that became a Latin organ-word, then a medieval verb, and English adds the endings that name the act and the person.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语的「工具」名词，先变成拉丁语的「器官」词，再变成中世纪的动词，英语又加上词尾来指行为与人。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon, Latin organum and medieval Latin organizare are all recorded, so this family has a reliable ancestry even though it crossed three languages.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 organon、拉丁语 organum 与中世纪拉丁语 organizare 均有记录，因此这一族词虽有三次跨语言，世系仍然可靠。

items.meaning: to arrange or form into a whole
the act of organizing, or a body so formed
to make, to put into a state

definition_zh: 起源；起点；出身；来源；原点
definition_en: the point at which something begins, the source from which it comes, or the fixed point of a coordinate system
core_image: 一条河从山间石缝里冒出第一股水，往下越流越宽
scene: 山谷尽头，向导蹲下身，指着石缝里冒出的第一股水，说明这条河从这里开始。The origin of the river lies in a spring high in the mountains.
sceneCN: 这里指「事物开始出现的地点或起点」（第 1 个义项：时间与空间上的开端）；句意为这条河的源头在高山中的一处泉水。图中可辨识物件：石缝、泉水、山谷、向导的手；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 起源；起点；出身；来源；原点

derivatives.zh: 起源；创始
最初的；原作
最初；原来
独创性

senses.title: The point where something begins
senses.definition: the place or moment at which something first exists or starts
senses.definitionCN: 某物首次存在或开始的地点或时刻
senses.example: The origin of the river lies in a spring high in the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河的源头在高山中的一处泉水。
senses.why: origo in Latin meant 'a beginning, a rising', from oriri 'to rise', so the word pictures something rising into existence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 origo 意为「开端、升起」，来自 oriri「升起」，因此这个词把事物想象为升起来而存在。

senses.title: Ancestry and social background
senses.definition: a person's family background or the place a family comes from
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的家庭背景或家族来处
senses.example: Her origin was a small farming village in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她的出身是北方一个小农村。
senses.why: a family's beginning is its first known place, so the word moved from places to people.
senses.whyCN: 家族的起点就是它最早可考的地方，于是这个词从地点移到了人身上。

senses.title: Source or provenance of a thing
senses.definition: the place or process a product or material comes from
senses.definitionCN: 产品或材料所来自的地方或过程
senses.example: The label records the origin of every bean in the bag.
senses.exampleCN: 标签记录袋中每颗豆子的原产地。
senses.why: trade needed a word for where goods begin their journey, and the general sense supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 贸易需要一个词来指货物开始旅程的地方，泛义正好提供了它。

senses.title: The origin of coordinates
senses.definition: the fixed point where the axes of a coordinate system meet
senses.definitionCN: 坐标系各轴相交的固定点
senses.example: The graph starts at the origin and rises to the right.
senses.exampleCN: 图像从原点开始，向右上升。
senses.why: mathematics borrowed the word for the zero point from which all positions are measured.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用了这个词，指一切位置由之量起的零点。

senses.title: The attachment point of a muscle
senses.definition: the end of a muscle that stays fixed when it contracts
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉收缩时保持不动的那一端
senses.example: The muscle's origin is on the pelvis and its insertion on the thigh.
senses.exampleCN: 这块肌肉的起点在骨盆，止点在大腿。
senses.why: anatomy reused the idea of a beginning for the fixed end from which a muscle acts.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把「开端」的观念用于肌肉发力的固定端。

senses.title: Etymology of a word
senses.definition: the earlier form and language from which a word derives
senses.definitionCN: 一个词所由来的更早形式与语言
senses.example: The dictionary gives the origin of the word in Latin.
senses.exampleCN: 词典给出这个词在拉丁语中的来源。
senses.why: a word's history begins somewhere, and that beginning is literally its origin.
senses.whyCN: 一个词的历史总有个开始，而那个开始字面上就是它的 origin。

senses.title: The first cause of an event
senses.definition: the earliest cause that set a chain of events going
senses.definitionCN: 启动一连串事件的最早原因
senses.example: Investigators traced the fire to an origin in faulty wiring.
senses.exampleCN: 调查者把火灾追溯到有问题的线路。
senses.why: causes form chains, and the first link is naturally called the origin.
senses.whyCN: 原因构成链条，第一环自然被称作 origin。

senses.title: Figurative root or source
senses.definition: a borrowed use for the deepest source of a feeling, problem or custom
senses.definitionCN: 借指情感、问题或习俗的最深根源
senses.example: The origin of their quarrel was a careless remark years before.
senses.exampleCN: 他们争吵的根源是多年前一句无心的话。
senses.why: the physical starting point became the image for whatever lies beneath a visible effect.
senses.whyCN: 物理起点成了可见结果之下一切东西的意象。

intro.en: Origin comes from Latin origo 'beginning, source', from oriri 'to rise'. It entered English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: origin 来自拉丁 origo「开端、来源」，后者出自动词 oriri「升起」，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oriri meant 'to rise, arise', used of the sun and of anything coming into being. Its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: oriri 意为「升起、出现」，用于太阳与任何开始存在的事物。其更深来源不确定。

items.en: Origo, originis meant 'a beginning, a source, a birth', and supplied the whole family of English words.
items.cn: origo, originis 意为「开端、来源、诞生」，提供了英语整组同族词。

items.en: Old French origine carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of a source or birth.
items.cn: 古法语 origine 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指来源或诞生。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word named the zero point of coordinate axes.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个词指坐标轴的零点。

items.en: Anatomy adopted origin for the fixed end of a muscle, extending the family into medicine.
items.cn: 解剖学采用 origin 指肌肉的固定端，把词族扩展到医学。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Latin source of oriri is not established, and any Indo-European root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：oriri 在拉丁语之前的来源未得到证明，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the look-alike nouns built on the same stem; group two holds near-meaning source words.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干构成的形近名词；第二组是语义相近的来源词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'first' or the first version of a work; origin is the starting point itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「最初的」的形容词，或作品的最初版本；origin 是起点本身。

entries.definition: To begin or to bring something into being; it names the event, not the point.
entries.definitionCN: 开始或使某物产生；它指事件，而非那个点。

entries.definition: The quality of being new and inventive; it has moved far from the sense of a beginning.
entries.definitionCN: 新颖而有创造性的品质；已远离「开端」之义。

entries.definition: The process of coming into being; origin is the point, origination is the process.
entries.definitionCN: 产生的过程；origin 是那个点，origination 是过程。

entries.definition: The place, person or thing from which something is obtained; it stresses supply rather than first existence.
entries.definitionCN: 获得某物的地点、人或物；强调供给，而非首次存在。

entries.definition: The first part or first moment of anything; it is the everyday equivalent of origin.
entries.definitionCN: 任何事物的最初部分或最初时刻；是 origin 的日常对应词。

entries.definition: The underlying cause or base of something, often figurative, as the root of a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 事物的深层原因或基础，常为比喻，如问题的根源。

entries.definition: The place where a person or movement was born; it is concrete and geographical.
entries.definitionCN: 人或运动诞生之地；具体且地理性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin pieces and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分与真实固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oriri 'to rise' plus -go gives 'a rising, a beginning'.
normal.cn: oriri「升起」加 -go 即「升起、开端」。

normal.en: The family runs origin, originate, original, originality, originator.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 origin、originate、original、originality、originator。

normal.en: Country of origin is a fixed trade phrase.
normal.cn: 原产国是固定的贸易短语。

normal.en: The origin of coordinates is the zero point of the axes.
normal.cn: 坐标原点是各轴的零点。

normal.en: Anatomy uses origin for the fixed end of a muscle.
normal.cn: 解剖学用 origin 指肌肉的固定端。

abstract.en: Picture the first thread of water coming out of a rock.
abstract.cn: 想象第一缕水从岩石缝里冒出来。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree whose lowest branch is a village.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家谱树，最下面的枝条是一个村庄。

abstract.en: Picture a quarrel that began with one careless sentence years ago.
abstract.cn: 想象一场争吵，始于多年前一句无心的话。

examples.en: The origin of the custom is lost.
examples.cn: 这一习俗的起源已经失传。

examples.en: The map marks the origin of every shipment.
examples.cn: 地图标出每批货物的来源地。

examples.en: The graph crosses the origin at zero.
examples.cn: 图像在零点穿过原点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ori（升起）+ gin（开端）」——事物升起来的那个点 → 起源、起点

root: 拉丁 origo, originis「开端、来源」，来自 oriri「升起」；oriri 更深来源不确定，其印欧词根一说属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rising point: where a thing begins, where a family begins, where goods come from, the zero of axes, the fixed end of a muscle, a word's history, the first cause and the hidden root.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个「升起的点」：事物开始处、家族开始处、货物来处、坐标零点、肌肉固定端、词的历史、最初原因与隐藏根源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first thread of water rising out of a rock and widening into a river.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一缕水从石缝里升起，逐渐变宽成一条河。

branches.en: BEGINNING AND CAUSE: the first moment and the first cause share one shape.
branches.cn: 开端与原因：最初时刻与最初原因共享同一形状。

branches.en: FAMILY: a person's beginning is a place and a lineage.
branches.cn: 家族：人的开始既是地点，也是血脉。

branches.en: PROVENANCE: goods and words both come from somewhere.
branches.cn: 来源：货物与词都从某处来。

branches.en: FIXED POINTS: axes and muscles need a point that does not move.
branches.cn: 固定点：坐标轴与肌肉都需要一个不动的点。

branches.en: ROOT: the hidden source beneath a visible effect.
branches.cn: 根源：可见结果之下的隐藏来源。

intro.en: Origin is a Latin noun whose stem recurs through a large English family.

definition_zh: 最初的；原来的；原创的；原件；原作；真迹的
definition_en: existing from the beginning, newly made and not copied from anything else, or the first version of something from which copies are made

scene: 老城区的档案馆里，管理员戴着薄手套，把一封旧信从纸盒中取出，信的纸边已经发黄。The letter in the glass case is an original, not a copy.

senses.title: Existing from the beginning
senses.definition: present at the start of something and not added or changed later
senses.definitionCN: 在某事开始时就已存在，后来既未添加也未改动的
senses.example: The original plan was much simpler than the final one.
senses.exampleCN: 最初的方案比最终方案简单得多。
senses.why: The Latin verb oriri means to rise, so the original thing is the one that stood at the rising point before anything else was laid on top of it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 oriri 意为升起，所以「最初的」那个东西，是站在起点上的那一个，其后的东西都还没有叠加上去。

senses.title: New and not copied from anything else
senses.definition: made by a particular mind rather than taken from an existing work or model
senses.definitionCN: 由某个头脑自己造出，而不是取自已有的作品或样板
senses.example: Her design for the bridge is completely original.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这座桥做的设计完全是原创的。
senses.why: If the source is the beginning, then a work that starts something new is itself a beginning, and the word turns from first in time to first of its kind.
senses.whyCN: 既然源头意味着开始，那么一件开创新东西的作品本身就是一个开始，这个词便从「时间上最早」转成「同类中最早」。

senses.title: The first version from which copies are made
senses.definition: the actual first document, artwork or object that later copies reproduce
senses.definitionCN: 后来各种复制品所依据的第一份真实文件、艺术原作或物件
senses.example: The museum keeps the original of the letter in a dark room.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把这封信的原件存放在一间暗室里。
senses.why: A copy needs a point of origin to be measured against, and English gives that first object the adjective as a noun: the original.
senses.whyCN: 复制品需要一个源头来对照，英语干脆把这个形容词当名词用，指那第一件东西：原件。

senses.title: Genuine, not a reproduction
senses.definition: made by the artist or maker themselves rather than produced later by someone else
senses.definitionCN: 由艺术家或制作者本人完成，而不是后人仿制或印刷的
senses.example: The painting on the wall is an original, not a print.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上那幅画是真迹，不是印刷品。
senses.why: Once the word marks the first object, it also marks what is real about it: whatever lacks that first hand is only a copy.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词标出那第一件东西，它也标出了这件东西的真实之处：凡缺少最初那只手的，就只是复制品。

intro.en: Original goes back to a Latin verb meaning to rise, and its noun for a beginning; the adjective then passed through French into English, where it also became a noun for the first object itself.
intro.cn: original 上溯到拉丁语中意为「升起」的动词及其表示「开始」的名词；这个形容词经法语进入英语，后来又兼作名词，指那第一件东西本身。

items.en: Oriri meant to rise or to come into being, and it was said of the sun rising as well as of anything that begins.
items.cn: oriri 意为升起、开始存在，既用于太阳升起，也用于任何开始出现的事物。

items.en: The noun origo, with the stem origin-, named a beginning or a source, the point from which a thing rises.
items.cn: 名词 origo 的词干为 origin-，指开端或源头，即事物由之升起的那一点。

items.en: Originalis described what belongs to the beginning or to the source rather than to a later copy.
items.cn: originalis 形容属于开端或源头的东西，而不是属于后来复制品的东西。

items.en: Old French used original for the first form of a thing, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century with that sense.
items.cn: 古法语用 original 指一件事物的最初形态，英语在十四世纪借入时也带来这个意思。

items.en: Modern English keeps original for what comes first in time, for work that is newly made, and for the very object from which copies are taken.
items.cn: 现代英语让 original 兼指时间上最早的、新造而非抄袭的，以及复制所依据的那件实物。

normalIntro.en: Original is an adjective built on the Latin noun for a source, so its hooks follow the moment a thing rises rather than any finished object.
normalIntro.cn: original 是建立在拉丁语「源头」名词上的形容词，所以记忆钩子顺着事物升起的那一刻走，而不是顺着任何成品走。

normal.en: Oriri is the Latin verb to rise, and original names what stood at that rising point before anything else came.
normal.cn: oriri 是拉丁语中表示「升起」的动词，而 original 指在那升起之点上、别的东西尚未到来时就已经存在的那一个。

normal.en: Origin is the noun of the same verb, and original is its adjective, so the pair keeps one stem in origin-.
normal.cn: origin 是同一动词的名词，original 是它的形容词，两者共用一个词干 origin-。

normal.en: The ending -al means belonging to, so original literally means belonging to the origin.
normal.cn: 词尾 -al 表示「属于……的」，所以 original 字面上就是「属于源头的」。

normal.en: The original meaning of a word is its oldest sense, while an original idea is one nobody had before, and the same word covers both kinds of first.
normal.cn: the original meaning 指一个词最老的义项，而 an original idea 指没人想到过的想法，同一个词兼指两种「第一」。

normal.en: An original painting is not a print because the word insists on the first object, not on the many copies made after it.
normal.cn: an original painting 不是印刷品，因为这个词强调的是第一件东西，而不是其后做出的许多复制品。

abstract.en: A word for the moment of rising suggests that originality is not decoration but a beginning someone had to make.
abstract.cn: 一个指向「升起那一刻」的词说明：原创不是装饰，而是有人必须做出的一个开端。

abstract.en: Every copy quietly points back to an original, even when nobody remembers who made the first one.
abstract.cn: 每一件复制品都默默指向一个原件，即便没人记得第一件是谁做的。

abstract.en: First in time and first of its kind are two different honours, and English lets one word carry both.
abstract.cn: 时间上的最早与同类中的首创是两种不同的光荣，而英语让一个词同时承担。

senses.title: At the beginning of something
senses.definition: at the time when something started, before later events changed it
senses.definitionCN: 在某事刚开始的时候，其后的事件尚未改变它
senses.example: Originally, the firm had only three employees.
senses.exampleCN: 起初，这家公司只有三名员工。
senses.why: The adverb is original plus -ly, and original goes back to the Latin verb oriri, to rise, so originally points at the very moment a thing rose into being.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词是 original 加 -ly，而 original 上溯拉丁语动词 oriri（升起），所以 originally 指向一件事物刚升起的那个时刻。

senses.title: In an earlier state, before later changes
senses.definition: as something was at an earlier period, in contrast with what it has since become
senses.definitionCN: 指某物在较早时期的样子，与它后来的样子相对照
senses.example: The house was originally a small school.
senses.exampleCN: 这所房子原先是一所小学校。
senses.why: If the word marks the first moment, it can also mark the whole earlier state that the first moment led into, which is how it comes to mean what a thing used to be.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词标出最初的那一刻，它也能标出那一刻所引出的整个早期状态，于是便能表示一件东西从前是什么样子。

senses.title: From a particular place or family origin
senses.definition: used with from to name the place where a person was born or began living
senses.definitionCN: 与 from 连用，指出一个人出生或最初生活的地方
senses.example: She is originally from a town in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她原籍是北方的一座小镇。
senses.why: A person also has a starting point, and the same adverb names that place of origin, turning the time sense into a sense of place.
senses.whyCN: 人也有自己的起点，同一个副词便用来指那个来源之地，把时间的意味转成了地点的意味。

senses.title: In a new and uncopied way
senses.definition: in a manner that shows fresh thought rather than following an existing model
senses.definitionCN: 以显出新鲜想法、而非照搬现成样板的方式
senses.example: The room was decorated originally, with colours nobody expected.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子的装饰很有独创性，用了没人想到的颜色。
senses.why: The adjective original also means not copied, and the adverb carries that sense into manner: to act originally is to begin something rather than repeat it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 original 也有「非复制」的意思，副词把这一层带入方式：以原创方式行事，就是开一个头，而不是重复别人。

intro.en: Originally is the adjective original with the adverb ending -ly; the adjective itself came from Latin through French, so the adverb carries the noun's idea of a starting point into the way a statement is qualified.
intro.cn: originally 是形容词 original 加上副词词尾 -ly；这个形容词本身经法语来自拉丁语，因此副词把「起点」的意思带进了句子的限定方式。

items.en: Oriri meant to rise or to come into being, and it pictured the first moment of anything that begins.

items.en: The noun origo, stem origin-, named the beginning or source from which a thing rises.

items.en: Originalis described what belongs to that beginning rather than to any later copy.

items.en: English joined original with -ly, the ending that turns an adjective into an adverb, and used the result for what was true at the start.
items.cn: 英语把 original 与 -ly 结合，这个词尾把形容词变成副词，并用它表示在开始时为真的事。

items.en: Modern English uses originally for the first moment, for an earlier state, for a place of origin, and for doing something in a new way.
items.cn: 现代英语让 originally 兼指最初的一刻、从前的状态、来源之地，以及以新方式做事。

normal.en: Originally planned and originally intended both mark what someone meant before the plan changed.

normal.en: The adverb often opens a sentence with a comma because it sets the time frame for everything that follows.

abstract.en: A word about the first moment reminds us that every present state was once a beginning someone chose.

abstract.en: Saying where someone is originally from is a way of telling a story that starts before the person can remember.

abstract.en: To do something originally is to refuse the copy, and the adverb makes that refusal a manner rather than a thing.

definition_zh: 否则；不然；在其他方面；除此之外；以别的方式
definition_en: in a different way, in other respects, or as the other result that follows if something does not happen
core_image: 一条路在岔口分成两支，一块木牌倒在左边，指向右边的那条路几乎没人走过
scene: 末班车的时间已经过了，站台上只剩一个人，他看了看表，又看了看暗下来的街口。You should leave now, otherwise you will miss the last train.
sceneCN: 这里的 otherwise 是「否则、不然」（第 1 个义项：如果不这样，就会有另一种结果）；句意为你现在就该走，否则会错过末班车。图中可辨识物件：站台、手表、暗下的街口。

senses.title: If not this, then something else will happen
senses.definition: used to say what will happen if the action just mentioned is not taken
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出若不做刚提到的那件事，就会出现另一种结果
senses.example: You should leave now, otherwise you will miss the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 你现在就该走，否则会错过末班车。
senses.why: The word began as an Old English phrase meaning in other ways, so the second clause describes the other way things can go.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是一句古英语短语，意为「以别的方式」，所以后一个分句说的就是事情可能走的另一种方式。

senses.title: In other respects, apart from what was just said
senses.definition: used to add that something is true apart from the one point already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 用来补充说明，除了刚才提到的那一点之外，其他方面是成立的
senses.example: The room is small but otherwise comfortable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间虽小，其他方面却舒适。
senses.why: If the phrase means in other ways, it can also mean with regard to other matters, and that is how it moves from a condition to an exception.
senses.whyCN: 既然这句话意为「以别的方式」，它也就能指「就其他事情而言」，于是从假设的条件转成了例外的补充。

senses.title: In a different way, not like that
senses.definition: in another manner, especially when the manner just thought of was not possible
senses.definitionCN: 以另一种方式，尤指刚想到的那种方式并不可行时
senses.example: There was no choice; he could not have acted otherwise.
senses.exampleCN: 当时别无选择，他不可能有别的做法。
senses.why: The oldest sense survives intact here: otherwise simply says by another way, without implying any condition or exception.
senses.whyCN: 最老的意思在这里完好地保留下来：otherwise 只说明「用另一种方式」，既不表条件，也不表例外。

intro.en: Otherwise is a frozen Old English phrase, on other wise, meaning in other ways; the two words fused into one adverb, and English later also used it as a conjunction.
intro.cn: otherwise 是一句凝固下来的古英语短语，原文意为「以别的方式」；两个词合成一个副词，英语后来又把它用作连词。

items.en: Other came from Old English oþer, meaning the second of two or simply a different one.
items.cn: other 来自古英语 oþer，意为两者中的另一个，或只是「不同的那一个」。

items.en: Wise was an old noun for manner or way, unrelated to the adjective meaning clever, and it survives in words such as likewise.
items.cn: wise 是表示方式、样子的古老名词，与表示「聪明」的形容词无关，它还活在 likewise 这类词里。

items.en: The phrase on oþre wisan meant in other ways, and it was used to describe an alternative course of action.
items.cn: 短语 on oþre wisan 意为「以别的方式」，用来描述另一种做法。

items.en: Middle English wrote the phrase as a single word, otherwise, and widened it to mean in other respects as well.
items.cn: 中古英语把这句短语写成一个词 otherwise，并把意思扩展到「在其他方面」。

items.en: Modern English uses otherwise as an adverb and a conjunction, with fixed phrases such as or otherwise and otherwise known as.
items.cn: 现代英语让 otherwise 兼作副词与连词，并有 or otherwise、otherwise known as 等固定说法。

normal.en: Wise here is an old noun for manner, not the adjective for clever, which is why otherwise has nothing to do with being smart.
normal.cn: 这里的 wise 是表示方式的古老名词，而不是表示「聪明」的形容词，所以 otherwise 与聪明无关。

normal.en: The same -wise family gives likewise and clockwise, both of which name a way of doing or going.
normal.cn: 同一个 -wise 词族还给出 likewise 与 clockwise，两者都指做事或行进的方式。

normal.en: Otherwise known as is the fixed phrase for a second name, and or otherwise pairs with or to cover remaining cases.
normal.cn: otherwise known as 是表示「另一个名字」的固定说法，而 or otherwise 与 or 连用，覆盖剩下的情况。

normal.en: As a conjunction it joins two clauses: do this, otherwise that will happen, which is why it often sits mid-sentence.
normal.cn: 作连词时它连接两个分句：做这个，否则就会那样，所以它常出现在句子中间。

abstract.en: A word that means in other ways quietly admits that every choice closes off another path.
abstract.cn: 一个意为「以别的方式」的词，默默承认每个选择都关上了另一条路。

abstract.en: The second name of a place or person is often hidden behind otherwise known as, a phrase doing the work of a footnote.
abstract.cn: 一个地方或一个人的第二个名字，常常藏在 otherwise known as 后面，这个短语干着脚注的活。

abstract.en: To say a thing is fine otherwise is to hold the good and the bad in one short sentence.
abstract.cn: 说一件东西除此之外都不错，就是用一句很短的话同时握住好与坏。

definition_zh: 盎司；少量；一点点；一丝
definition_en: a unit of weight of about twenty-eight grams, with a heavier troy form used for precious metals; also a very small amount or the slightest trace of a quality
core_image: 旧药铺柜台上的一台小铜天平，一端放着待称的小块黄油，另一端是小小的砝码
scene: 旧药铺的柜台上摆着一台小铜天平，药剂师把一小块黄油放上砝码盘，铜指针慢慢停住。The old recipe asks for one ounce of butter and a pinch of salt.
sceneCN: 这里 ounce 是「盎司」（第 1 个义项：常衡重量单位）；句意为老配方要一盎司黄油加一撮盐，画面是药铺柜台上那台停住的小铜天平。

pos.zh: 盎司；少量；一丝

senses.title: A unit of weight equal to about twenty-eight grams
senses.definition: a unit of weight used in ordinary trade, equal to one sixteenth of a pound or about 28.35 grams
senses.definitionCN: 用于一般贸易的重量单位，等于十六分之一磅，约二十八点三五克
senses.example: Add four ounces of flour to the bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 往碗里加四盎司面粉。
senses.why: Latin uncia named a twelfth part of a larger unit, so the word began as a fraction cut off from something bigger; trade later fixed that fraction into the everyday ounce of sixteen to the pound.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 uncia 本指某一较大单位的十二分之一，所以这个词一开始是「从大单位切下的一份」；后来贸易把这个分数固定成十六分之一磅的日常盎司，分数观念就变成了具体的称重单位。

senses.title: A troy unit used for precious metals
senses.definition: a unit of weight of about 31.1 grams, used for gold, silver and other precious metals
senses.definitionCN: 约三十一点一克的重量单位，用于黄金、白银等贵金属
senses.example: Gold is traded by the troy ounce on world markets.
senses.exampleCN: 黄金在国际市场上按金衡盎司交易。
senses.why: The older twelve-part division survived in the bullion trade after ordinary goods moved to a sixteen-part pound, so one name ended up covering two slightly different weights.
senses.whyCN: 日常货物改用十六分之一磅之后，旧式十二分之一的分法仍在金银交易里活着；同一个名字于是同时指两种略不相同的重量，贵金属这一支保留了更重的古制。

senses.title: A very small quantity
senses.definition: a very small amount of something, often used to stress how little is left or present
senses.definitionCN: 某物极少的一点，常用于强调所剩或所有之少
senses.example: There was not an ounce of sugar left in the jar.
senses.exampleCN: 罐子里一点糖都不剩了。
senses.why: An ounce sits near the bottom of a kitchen scale, so the name of the smallest readable weight drifts easily into a word for a scrap of anything.
senses.whyCN: 盎司落在厨房秤刻度的最低处，于是这个「最小可读重量」的名称很容易滑成「随便一点什么」的说法；义项由称量的下限转向数量上的极小。

senses.title: The slightest trace of a quality
senses.definition: a small but real amount of a feeling or quality, as in an ounce of courage or not an ounce of sense
senses.definitionCN: 某种情感或品质虽少却真实的一点，如「一丝勇气」或「毫无理智」
senses.example: He did not show an ounce of regret for what he had done.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己做过的事没有表现出一丝悔意。
senses.why: The smallest weight is borrowed to weigh what cannot be put on a scale, so an ounce of a quality means just enough of it to count.
senses.whyCN: 最小的重量被借去称无法放上天平的东西，所以「一丝某种品质」就是刚好够算数的那一点；这次转移靠的是用称重词去量看不见的性情。

intro.en: Ounce descends from a Latin word for a twelfth part, and the same source also gave English inch, which is why a weight and a length share a name.
intro.cn: ounce 上溯自一个表示「十二分之一」的拉丁词，同一来源还给出了英语的 inch，所以一种重量与一种长度共用一段来历。

items.en: Uncia named a twelfth part of a pound or of any larger unit, and it is also the source of the English inch.
items.cn: uncia 指一磅或任何较大单位的十二分之一，也是英语 inch 的来源。

items.en: Old French shortened the Latin word to unce, the form English borrowed for a small weight.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁词缩为 unce，英语借入时用它指一种小重量。

items.en: Middle English kept the word for a small weight and for a twelfth part, and merchants used it alongside the pound.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词指小重量，也指十二分之一，商人们把它与磅并用。

items.en: When the sixteen-ounce pound became standard for ordinary goods, the older twelve-part unit stayed in the bullion trade, so one name covered two weights.
items.cn: 当十六盎司为一磅的常衡制成为普通货物的标准，旧的十二进制单位仍留在金银交易中，同一个名字于是覆盖了两种重量。

items.en: Modern English uses ounce for the everyday measure, the troy measure for metals, and figuratively for a very small amount of anything.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ounce 指日常重量、贵金属的金衡重量，也引申指任何东西的极小量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin twelfth-part word and two words that merely rhyme with ounce; the near-meaning group gathers units of weight and words for a tiny amount.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「十二分之一」一词上的形式，以及两个只是读音相近的词；近义组收重量单位与表示极小量的词。

entries.definition: A unit of length, also descended from Latin uncia, a twelfth part.
entries.definitionCN: 长度单位英寸，同样出自拉丁语 uncia（十二分之一）。

entries.definition: A style of large rounded writing, named from a Latin adjective meaning a twelfth of a foot in height.
entries.definitionCN: 一种大写圆体字，名称出自意为「十二分之一英尺高」的拉丁形容词。

entries.definition: To make something known publicly; the ending looks like ounce but the word comes from Latin nuntius, a messenger.
entries.definitionCN: 公开宣告；词尾看似盎司，实际出自拉丁语 nuntius（信使），只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To spring back after hitting a surface; the spelling echoes ounce but the word is probably imitative and unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 碰到表面后弹回；拼写与盎司相近，但一般认为出自模仿声音，来源不同。

entries.definition: A metric unit of weight equal to one thousandth of a kilogram.
entries.definitionCN: 公制重量单位，等于千分之一千克。

entries.definition: A unit of weight made of sixteen ounces, or twelve in the troy system.

entries.definition: A very small amount of something that is barely there.

entries.definition: An extremely small amount, used especially in negative statements.
entries.definitionCN: 极微小的一点，尤用于否定句。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a Latin fraction, a trade weight and a figure of speech, so its hooks return to cutting, weighing and the smallest measurable share.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着一个拉丁分数、一个贸易重量和一种说法，记忆钩子都回到切分、称量与最小可称的一份。

normal.en: Uncia meant a twelfth part, so ounce began as a fraction rather than a fixed weight.
normal.cn: uncia 意为十二分之一，所以 ounce 起初是个分数，而不是固定的重量。

normal.en: The same Latin word gave inch, because both were cut from a larger unit by the same habit of dividing into twelve.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词还给出 inch，因为两者都是按十二等分的老习惯从大单位里切出来的。

normal.en: Troy and avoirdupois are two ways of cutting the pound, and ounce simply followed both.
normal.cn: 金衡与常衡是把磅切成两套办法，ounce 两套都跟着用。

normal.en: Kitchen scales read in ounces, which is why the word can mean a very small amount of anything.
normal.cn: 厨房秤以盎司读数，所以这个词可以指任何东西的极小量。

normal.en: An ounce of courage is the unit turned into a moral measure, weighing a quality on the same scale.
normal.cn: an ounce of courage 是把单位变成品性的量尺，用同一杆秤去称一种性情。

abstract.en: A brass scale on a pharmacy counter, one weight on each pan, is the word at its plainest.
abstract.cn: 药铺柜台上一台铜天平、两盘各放一个砝码，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A gold bar on a dealer's tray is the same name made heavier by old custom.

abstract.en: A cook adding a single spoonful to a bowl shows a weight unit shrinking into a pinch.

examples.cn: 这份配方要求一盎司黄油。

examples.en: Gold is sold by the troy ounce in most markets.
examples.cn: 多数市场上黄金按金衡盎司出售。

examples.en: He did not show an ounce of regret.
examples.cn: 他没有表现出一丝悔意。

definition_zh: 我们自己；我们亲自；独自；私下地
definition_en: the reflexive pronoun used when the subject we acts on itself, and the emphatic form that stresses that we personally did something
core_image: 几个人围着一张搬进教室的旧桌子，四下张望，确认没有别人在帮忙
scene: 周末的教室空了下来，几个人自己搬桌子、刷墙，没有叫校工过来搭手。We painted the whole classroom ourselves, without asking the caretaker for help.
sceneCN: 这里 ourselves 是「靠我们自己」（第 3 个义项：by ourselves，表示不借助外人）；句意为一整间教室由我们自刷完，画面是空教室里围着一张旧桌子的几个人。

pos.zh: 我们自己；我们亲自；独自；私下地

derivatives.zh: 由 our 与 self 合写而成，是 ourselves 的单数形式，现仅见于王室或极正式的文字
古英语 self，义为「自身、本人」，是这一族反身形式的共同词干
由 self 与 same 复合而成，义为「完全相同的」

senses.title: The reflexive form of we
senses.definition: used as the object of a verb or preposition when the subject is we and the object is the same group of people
senses.definitionCN: 当主语是 we、而宾语恰恰是同一群人时，用作动词或介词的宾语
senses.example: We taught ourselves to play the guitar.
senses.exampleCN: 我们自学弹吉他。
senses.why: English sends an action back to its source with the self-words, so ourselves keeps the doing inside the very group that started it.
senses.whyCN: 英语用 self 这一族形式把动作送回它的来源，所以 ourselves 让「做」留在这群发起者内部；反身义就是「宾语与主语同指一批人」的直接结果。

senses.title: Used to stress that we personally did something
senses.definition: placed after we or at the end of a clause to insist that the people named did it in person
senses.definitionCN: 放在 we 之后或句末，强调所说的正是我们这批人亲自做的
senses.example: We built the whole shed ourselves.
senses.exampleCN: 整个棚子都是我们亲手搭的。
senses.why: The same form that bends the action back can also stand beside the subject as a pointer, so it adds weight instead of a new object.
senses.whyCN: 同一个能把动作折回自身的形式，也能站到主语旁边充当指示，于是它增加的是分量而不是新的宾语；强调义来自反身形式离开宾语位置之后的用法。

senses.title: Without help from anyone else
senses.definition: used in the phrase by ourselves to mean alone, or with no outside person assisting
senses.definitionCN: 用在 by ourselves 这一短语中，表示独自，或没有外人在旁帮忙
senses.example: We finished the repair by ourselves.
senses.exampleCN: 那次修理是我们自己完成的。
senses.why: If a group acts only within itself, no outside hand is involved, so the reflexive phrase settles into the meaning of unaided.
senses.whyCN: 如果一群人只在自己人内部使力，就没有外人的手参与，于是这个反身短语安定成「无人相助」的意思；独立义是从「不让别人插手」推出来的。

senses.title: Kept private among the speakers
senses.definition: used in between ourselves to mark that something is said in confidence and should not go further
senses.definitionCN: 用在 between ourselves 中，标记话语是私下讲的，不该再往外传
senses.example: Between ourselves, the plan has already been dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 私下说，这个计划其实已经取消了。
senses.why: A group closed upon itself is also a circle of trust, so the reflexive form can mark words meant to stay inside that circle.
senses.whyCN: 一个只向自己人闭合的群体，同时也是一个信任的圈子，所以这个反身形式能标记只该留在圈内的话；私密义由「闭合的小圈子」这一画面长出。

intro.en: Ourselves is our plus selves, a pronoun welded to the plural of self; the deeper origin of self is reconstructed rather than recorded.
intro.cn: ourselves 是 our 加 selves，也就是一个代词与 self 的复数焊在一起；self 更早的来源是重构出来的，而非有文字记录。

items.en: A reflexive stem usually reconstructed as sel-bho- is thought to lie behind the self-words, though the exact form remains uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为，self 一族背后有一个重构为 sel-bho- 的反身词干，但确切形式仍不确定。

items.en: The reconstructed selbaz gave the Germanic languages their word for self, used both alone and beside pronouns.
items.cn: 重构形式 selbaz 为日耳曼诸语提供了表示「自身」的词，既可单用，也可放在代词旁边。

items.en: Old English set the pronoun and self side by side as separate words to say that the group acted on itself.
items.cn: 古英语把代词与 self 作为两个词并排使用，表示这群人把动作施于自身。

items.en: Middle English drew the parts together with the possessive our, and the plural selves won out so the form matched the plural subject.
items.cn: 中古英语用所有格 our 把两部分连写，复数形式 selves 占了上风，以便与复数主语相配。

items.en: Modern English fixed ourselves as the reflexive and emphatic form of we, leaving ourself to royal and very formal use.
items.cn: 现代英语把 ourselves 固定为 we 的反身与强调形式，只把 ourself 留给王室与极正式的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the other members of the same self-paradigm; the near-meaning group gathers plain pronouns and a phrase that carries the idea of acting alone.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个 self 系列里的其他成员；近义组收普通代词与一个表示「独自行动」的短语。

entries.definition: The reflexive form used when the subject is you.
entries.definitionCN: 主语是 you 时所用的反身形式。

entries.definition: The reflexive form used when the subject is they.
entries.definitionCN: 主语是 they 时所用的反身形式。

entries.definition: The reflexive form used when the subject is I.
entries.definitionCN: 主语是 I 时所用的反身形式。

entries.definition: A singular form once used with we in royal or formal speech and now rarely seen.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时在王室或正式文书中与 we 连用的单数形式，现已罕见。

entries.definition: The object form of we, a plain pronoun with no self idea.
entries.definitionCN: we 的宾格形式，是普通代词，不含「自身」之意。

entries.definition: The subject pronoun for the speaker together with at least one other person.
entries.definitionCN: 说话者与至少另一位构成的主语代词。

entries.definition: The possessive pronoun meaning belonging to us.
entries.definitionCN: 表示属于我们的物主代词。

entries.definition: Without help or support from anyone else.
entries.definitionCN: 没有别人帮助或支持；靠自己。

normalIntro.en: The word is our glued to the plural of self, so its hooks return to the group, to the self that turns back, and to the circle that keeps others out.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 our 与 self 的复数粘在一起，记忆钩子都回到这群人、折回自身的那个 self，以及把外人挡在外的圈子。

normal.en: Our means belonging to us, and selves is the plural of self, so the two halves say the same group twice.
normal.cn: our 意为属于我们，selves 是 self 的复数，两个部分把同一群人说了两遍。

normal.en: The self-forms are what English uses when the object of a verb is the subject itself, and ourselves fills that slot for we.
normal.cn: 凡是动词的宾语就是主语本身时，英语就用 self 这一族形式，而 ourselves 为 we 补上这个位置。

normal.en: Move the same form next to the subject and it stops being an object, which is how the emphatic use is born.
normal.cn: 把同一形式挪到主语旁边，它就不再是宾语，强调用法就是这样产生的。

normal.en: By ourselves keeps the group closed, so the phrase means alone, while between ourselves keeps talk inside the same circle.
normal.cn: by ourselves 把人群关起来，所以短语意为独自；between ourselves 则把话留在同一个圈内。

normal.en: Our own is the possessive echo of the same idea, since what belongs to us and what acts on us are both ours.
normal.cn: our own 是同一想法的所有格回声，因为属于我们的东西与对我们动手的东西都归我们。

abstract.en: A closed circle of people with no door for outsiders is the shape of by ourselves and between ourselves at once.
abstract.cn: 一圈人闭合成环、不给外人留门，就是 by ourselves 与 between ourselves 共同的形状。

abstract.en: A hand pointing back at the chest of the speaker shows the reflexive turn that the whole self-family marks.
abstract.cn: 一只手反指说话者的胸口，显示整个 self 系列所标记的那次折回。

abstract.en: A group carrying a table up the stairs with no one else on the steps is the word turned into a shared effort.
abstract.cn: 一群人自己把桌子抬上楼、台阶上没有别人，就是这个词变成共同出力时的样子。

examples.en: We taught ourselves to play the guitar.
examples.cn: 我们自学弹吉他。

examples.en: We built the whole shed ourselves.
examples.cn: 整个棚子都是我们亲手搭的。

examples.en: Between ourselves, the plan has already been dropped.
examples.cn: 私下说，这个计划其实已经取消了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥，塞住自己」——把外人挡在圈子外面，只留下我们自己。

root: 古英语以代词与 self 并列表意，中古英语把 our 与 self 的复数 selves 合写成 ourselves；self 一般认为上溯到原始日耳曼语 selbaz，更早的印欧形式不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a group turning an action back on itself; that picture splits into the plain reflexive, the emphatic pointer, the unaided group, and the circle of confidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一群人把动作折回自身；这幅画面分出普通反身、强调指示、无人相助的一群，以及只对内的信任圈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several people carrying a table into a classroom, looking round to check that nobody else is helping.
core.cn: 核心意象：几个人自己把桌子搬进教室，四下张望，确认没有别人在帮忙。

branches.en: a hand pointing back at the speaker's chest
branches.cn: 一只手反指说话者的胸口

branches.en: the same group named twice, once as doer and once as the one who did it in person
branches.cn: 同一群人被说两遍，一次作施动者，一次强调亲自所为

branches.en: a table carried upstairs with no one else on the steps
branches.cn: 没人搭手、自己抬上楼的桌子

branches.en: two people talking with the door shut
branches.cn: 关起门来说话的两个人

branches.en: effort with no outside hand, once stressed and once described
branches.cn: 没有外人之手的出力，一次用于强调，一次用于陈述

intro.en: The word is a pronoun plus the plural of self, set inside an English family of self-forms that mark an action returning to its doer.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个代词加上 self 的复数，嵌在英语一整套 self 形式之中，用来标记动作回到施动者本身。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
