definition_zh: 在外；向外；出去；熄灭；过时；从…出来
definition_en: away from the inside of a place, or moving from within to beyond a boundary; also no longer burning or fashionable; as a preposition, through and away from
core_image: 厨房的灯忽然灭了，一个人摸黑推开门，从屋里走到院子里
scene: 夜里厨房的灯忽然灭了，一个人摸黑推开门，从屋里走到院子里站定。The kitchen light went out while we were still washing the dishes.
sceneCN: 这里 out 是「熄灭」（第 3 个义项：火、灯或电器不再亮、不再工作）；句意为碗还没洗完，厨房的灯就灭了，画面是黑下来的厨房与走向院子的人。

pos.zh: 在外；向外；出去；熄灭；过时
从…出来；离开
过时的；不再流行的

derivatives.zh: 由 out 加比较级词尾 -er 构成，义为「外部的；外面的」
由 out 加 -ing 构成，义为「外出；短途游玩」
由 out 与 set 复合而成，义为「开始；开端」
由 outward 加副词词尾 -s 构成，义为「向外地」

senses.title: Away from inside a place
senses.definition: not inside a building, room or container, but beyond its boundary
senses.definitionCN: 不在建筑物、房间或容器之内，而处在它的边界之外
senses.example: She is out at the moment, so please call again later.
senses.exampleCN: 她这会儿出去了，请稍后再打。
senses.why: Old English ut simply named the far side of a boundary, so the word's first task is to say that something is not inside.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ut 只指边界之外的那一侧，所以这个词最初的任务就是说明某物不在里面；第一义是纯粹的空间否定，没有别的引申。

senses.title: Moving from within to outside
senses.definition: used with verbs of movement to show a passage from inside to beyond
senses.definitionCN: 与表示移动的动词连用，表示从里面穿到外面
senses.example: He walked out without saying a word.
senses.exampleCN: 他一句话没说就走了出去。
senses.why: If the word can name the far side, it can also name the step that reaches it, so verbs of motion take out as a direction.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指界外那一侧，也就能指跨到那一侧的那一步，所以表示移动的动词带上 out 就成了方向；静态位置由此转成动态离开。

senses.title: No longer burning or working
senses.definition: of a fire, lamp or device, no longer burning, shining or running
senses.definitionCN: 指火、灯或电器不再燃烧、不再发亮、不再运转
senses.example: The fire went out before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 火在午夜前就熄了。
senses.why: A flame that is out has left the state of burning, so the word for being beyond a boundary is applied to a condition that has ended.
senses.whyCN: 熄掉的火已经离开了燃烧的状态，于是这个表示「在界外」的词被用到一种已经结束的状态上；熄灭义就是把它从空间之外搬到状态之外。

senses.title: No longer fashionable
senses.definition: of a style or idea, no longer in fashion or no longer accepted
senses.definitionCN: 指样式或观念不再流行，或不再被接受
senses.example: Long skirts are out this season.
senses.exampleCN: 长裙这一季已经过时了。
senses.why: A style that falls outside the set of things people currently accept is literally out of that set, so the spatial word becomes a judgement of taste.
senses.whyCN: 一种样式落在人们当下接受的那一套之外，就字面地「不在这一套里」，于是空间词变成了品味判断；过时义靠的正是「圈外」这个画面。

senses.title: Through and away from
senses.definition: used before a noun, as in out the door or out of the room, to mark the way from inside to outside
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词之前，如 out the door 或 out of the room，标出从内到外的路径
senses.example: She ran out the door into the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她跑出门，冲进了雨里。
senses.why: The preposition keeps the same crossing but puts a noun after it, so out takes an object and names the opening that is passed through.
senses.whyCN: 介词用法保留同一次越界，只在后面接上名词，于是 out 带宾语，指被穿过的那道出口；词性变了，画面没有变。

intro.en: Out is one of the oldest English adverbs, and its history is a single idea, the far side of a boundary, spreading from place to condition and to fashion.
intro.cn: out 是英语最古老的副词之一，它的历史只有一个念头：边界之外的那一侧；这个念头从位置扩展到状态，再扩展到时尚。

items.en: The root usually reconstructed as ud- carried the sense of outward or upward movement, and it is the deepest layer behind the English word.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构为 ud- 的词根带有「向外、向上」的意思，是英语这个词最深的一层。

items.en: The reconstructed ut gave the Germanic languages an adverb for motion away from the inside.
items.cn: 重构形式 ut 为日耳曼诸语提供了一个表示「离开内部」的副词。

items.en: Old English ut was an adverb of place and direction, and it already appeared beside verbs of going and coming.
items.cn: 古英语 ut 是表示位置与方向的副词，已经常与来去的动词连用。

items.en: Middle English out widened from space to conditions, so a fire or a supply could be called out once it had ended.
items.cn: 中古英语把 out 从空间扩展到状态，火或供应一旦终结就可以说成 out。

items.en: Modern English adds the preposition use, the adjective sense of unfashionable, and a large family of compounds from outset to outlook.
items.cn: 现代英语补上介词用法、表示「过时」的形容词义，以及从 outset 到 outlook 的一大族复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the English out and one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers words for the outside position and for leaving.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在英语 out 上的形式，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示外面位置与离开的词。

entries.definition: On or near the outside of something.
entries.definitionCN: 在某物外部或靠近外部的。

entries.definition: A short trip taken for pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 为消遣而进行的短途出游。

entries.definition: To do better than another person.
entries.definitionCN: 做得比另一人更好；胜过。

entries.definition: Concerning, or roughly; the spelling resembles out but the word is built from a different Old English phrase meaning around.
entries.definitionCN: 关于，或大约；拼写与 out 相近，但由另一个古英语短语构成，意为「在周围」，词源不同。

entries.definition: The outer part or surface of something, or beyond the limits of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的外部或表面，也指在某个场所的界限之外。

entries.definition: At a distance from a person or place.
entries.definitionCN: 离开某人或某地，处在远处。

entries.definition: In the open air, not inside a building.
entries.definitionCN: 在露天，不在建筑物之内。

entries.definition: Towards the outside, or on the outer side.
entries.definitionCN: 朝向外面，或位于外侧。

normalIntro.en: The word is a single boundary picture with many uses, so its hooks return to the far side, the step across it, and the state that lies beyond.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是同一个边界画面的多种用法，记忆钩子都回到界外那一侧、跨过去的那一步，以及落在边界之外的状态。

normal.en: Old English ut marked the far side of a boundary, which is why out answers the plain question where.
normal.cn: 古英语 ut 标出边界的那一侧，所以 out 回答最朴素的「在哪里」。

normal.en: The same word covers the crossing as well as the position, so walk and run take it as a direction.
normal.cn: 同一个词既管位置也管越界，所以 walk 与 run 带上它就成了方向。

normal.en: A fire that has left the state of burning is called out, which shows the word moving from space to condition.
normal.cn: 离开燃烧状态的火被叫作 out，显示这个词从空间挪到了状态。

normal.en: Out of date and out of order share one shape: the thing has fallen outside the set of what still works.
normal.cn: out of date 与 out of order 形状相同：东西落到「还能用」的那一套之外了。

normal.en: Outer, outing and outset all keep the boundary picture, and only the part of speech changes.
normal.cn: outer、outing、outset 都保留着边界画面，变的只是词性。

abstract.en: A door standing open with a lamp still burning inside is the word's plainest picture.
abstract.cn: 一扇门开着、屋里灯还亮着，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A match going dark at the end of a stick is the moment out stops meaning place and starts meaning ended.
abstract.cn: 火柴在棒端熄灭的那一瞬，就是 out 从「位置」转成「结束」的时刻。

abstract.en: A hat left outside a shop window marks a style that has fallen out of favour.
abstract.cn: 一顶被搁在橱窗外的帽子，标记一种已经失宠的样式。

examples.en: The fire went out before midnight.
examples.cn: 火在午夜前就熄了。

examples.en: She is out at the moment.
examples.cn: 她这会儿出去了。

examples.en: Long skirts are out this season.
examples.cn: 长裙这一季已经过时了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「熬特」——熬到灯都灭了、人还在屋子外面；out 就是在外面，也是熄灭。

root: 古英语 ut（在外、向外）承自原始日耳曼语重构形式 ut，更早一般认为上溯到印欧词根 ud-；词义由空间上的「界外」扩展到状态上的「结束」与品味上的「过时」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the far side of a boundary; the senses move from that position, to the crossing, to a condition that has ended, to a style outside current taste, and to the preposition of passage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是边界之外的那一侧；义项从那个位置，转到跨越动作，转到已经终结的状态，转到落在当下品味之外的样式，再转到表穿越的介词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kitchen lamp dying while someone pushes the door open and steps from the dark room into the yard.
core.cn: 核心意象：厨房的灯灭了，有人推开门，从黑下来的屋子走到院子里。

branches.en: a lamp still burning in an empty room
branches.cn: 空屋里仍亮着的灯

branches.en: a man stepping through a doorway into the yard
branches.cn: 一个人穿过门口走进院子

branches.en: a fire dying to grey ash
branches.cn: 火渐渐熄成灰

branches.en: a long skirt pushed to the back of a wardrobe
branches.cn: 长裙被推到衣柜深处

branches.en: one crossing, once through a door and once through a word's syntax
branches.cn: 同一次越界，一次穿过门，一次穿过句式

intro.en: The word is an Old English adverb that grew into a prefix, an adjective and a large compound family, all on the same boundary picture.
intro.cn: 这个词是古英语的一个副词，后来长成前缀、形容词与一大族复合词，全部围绕同一个边界画面。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 结果；结局；成果；结局指标
definition_en: the result or final situation produced by an event, process, decision, or treatment
core_image: 一条路走到尽头，终点处落下一个清晰的印记
scene: 临床试验结束时，研究团队把两组康复率并排写进同一张表。The main outcome was clear: the treated group recovered twelve points more often than the control group.
sceneCN: 这里 outcome 是“（研究或临床的）结局指标”（第 8 个义项：统计意义上的终点指标）；句意：主要结局指标很清楚：用药组的康复率比对照组高出十二个百分点。图中可辨识物件：病历表、统计柱状图、药瓶、研究记录；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 结果；结局；成果
（研究／医疗）结局指标；终点

derivatives.zh: 结果；外出（古/罕用）
来；发生
收入（in + come，进来的东西）
克服；战胜
即将到来的；乐于提供信息的

senses.title: The result of an event or process
senses.definition: the result or final situation that follows from an event or process
senses.definitionCN: 由某个事件或过程产生的最终结果或局面
senses.example: The outcome of the experiment surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 实验的结果让所有人都感到意外。
senses.why: The word is a compound of out and come: something comes out of a process and stands at the end of it. The result is pictured as a thing that emerges and becomes visible once the process is finished.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 out 与 come 复合而成：某物从过程里“走出来”，停在过程的末端。结果被想象成一件在过程结束后浮现、变得可见的东西。

senses.title: A consequence of a decision
senses.definition: the effect that a decision or action has, often considered before it is made
senses.definitionCN: 某个决定或行动带来的效果，常在做出决定前就被考虑
senses.example: Before you speak, consider the outcome of your words.
senses.exampleCN: 开口之前，先想想你的话会带来什么后果。
senses.why: The same emergence is now read backwards as consequence: the decision sends something out, and that something returns as the situation you must live in.
senses.whyCN: 同样的“浮现”现在被反向读成后果：决定送出某样东西，而那样东西又作为你必须生活在其中的局面返回。

senses.title: The result of a contest or vote
senses.definition: the final result of an election, trial, game, or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 选举、审判、比赛或谈判的最终结果
senses.example: The outcome of the election remained unclear for days.
senses.exampleCN: 选举结果数日未明。
senses.why: A contest is a process with a single end point, so outcome fits it naturally. The word does not say who won; it names the shape the whole process leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 竞赛是一个有单一终点的过程，因此 outcome 天然适用。这个词不说明谁赢，只命名整个过程留下的那个形状。

senses.title: A medical or clinical result
senses.definition: the health result of a treatment or illness for a patient or group
senses.definitionCN: 治疗或疾病给患者或群体带来的健康结果
senses.example: Better hygiene led to improved patient outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 更好的卫生条件改善了患者的治疗结果。
senses.why: Medicine turns the everyday word into a measured endpoint: the process is treatment, and what comes out at the end is the patient's condition. The metaphor of emergence becomes a chart.
senses.whyCN: 医学把日常词变成可测量的终点：过程是治疗，末端“走出来”的是患者的状况。浮现的比喻变成了一张图表。

senses.title: The expected or desired result
senses.definition: the result that people hope for or predict, often stated in advance
senses.definitionCN: 人们希望或预测的结果，常被提前说明
senses.example: The negotiators aimed for a fair outcome for both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判者力求让双方都得到公平的结果。
senses.why: Once the end point is known to be a result, it can be wished for before it exists. The word stops describing what happened and starts naming a target placed at the end of the process.
senses.whyCN: 一旦知道末端是一个结果，它就可以在存在之前被期盼。这个词于是不再描述已发生的事，而是命名一个被放在过程末端的目标。

senses.title: A learning outcome in education
senses.definition: a specific skill or understanding that students are expected to gain from a course
senses.definitionCN: 学生预期从课程中获得的具体技能或理解
senses.example: Each lesson lists three learning outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 每节课都列出三项学习成果。
senses.why: Education reverses the direction: instead of asking what came out of teaching, it first declares what should come out. The outcome becomes a designed destination rather than a report.
senses.whyCN: 教育把方向倒过来：不是问教学之后“出来了什么”，而是先声明“应该出来什么”。结果由事后报告变成事先设计的目的地。

senses.title: The result of a legal case
senses.definition: the final decision or settlement of a legal dispute or court case
senses.definitionCN: 法律争议或法庭案件的最终裁决或和解
senses.example: The case outcome depended on one witness.
senses.exampleCN: 案件结果取决于一名证人。
senses.why: A trial is a bounded procedure with an official end, so its result is called an outcome rather than a mere effect. The word suits any process that is formally closed.
senses.whyCN: 审判是一个有官方终点的有限程序，因此它的结果被称为 outcome，而不只是 effect。这个词适用于任何正式结束的过程。

senses.title: A measured endpoint in research
senses.definition: a variable that researchers measure at the end of a study to judge whether an intervention worked
senses.definitionCN: 研究者在研究结束时测量、用来判断干预是否有效的变量
senses.example: Recovery rate was the primary outcome of the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 康复率是该试验的主要终点指标。
senses.why: Statistics narrows outcome to one measured thing among many possible results. The end of the process is now a designated variable, chosen before the data are collected so the question cannot be moved afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把 outcome 收窄为众多可能结果中被选定测量的一项。过程的末端现在是一个事先指定的变量，在收集数据前就定好，以免事后移动问题。

intro.en: Outcome is not Latin at all. It is a Scottish English compound of two native words, and its history shows the modern sense is surprisingly late.
intro.cn: outcome 根本不是拉丁词。它是两个英语本族词构成的苏格兰英语复合词，其历史显示现代义出现得相当晚。

items.en: c. 1200, out-coming was used for 'an emergence, act or fact of coming out'. Old English had utancumen 'stranger, foreigner', literally 'one who came from outside'.
items.cn: 约 1200 年，out-coming 表示“出现、出来的行为或事实”。古英语有 utancumen“陌生人、外来者”，字面是“从外面来的人”。

items.en: The noun outcome is recorded in 1788, originally Scottish, meaning 'that which results from something'. It comes from the verbal phrase out + come.
items.cn: 名词 outcome 记录于 1788 年，最初见于苏格兰，义为“由某事物产生的结果”。它来自动词短语 out + come。

items.en: Popularized in English by Thomas Carlyle around the 1830s, according to standard references.
items.cn: 据通行资料，托马斯·卡莱尔在 1830 年代前后使这个词在英语中流行开来。

items.en: The word stays a transparent compound: out (forth, into view) + come (arrive). Its force is that the result is something that came out and can now be seen.
items.cn: 这个词始终是透明的复合词：out（向外、进入视野）+ come（到达）。它的力量在于：结果是“走出来”、现在能被看见的东西。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine, education, and statistics turned outcome into a countable endpoint: patient outcome, learning outcome, primary outcome.
items.cn: 20 世纪的医学、教育与统计学把 outcome 变成可计数的终点：patient outcome、learning outcome、primary outcome。

note.en: The first group separates other out- compounds; the second ranks the main synonyms by where they place the result.
note.cn: 第一组把其他 out- 复合词分开；第二组按“结果被放在哪里”来区分主要近义词。

entries.definition: the amount produced by a machine, worker, or system. It is what is put out, not the situation that results.
entries.definitionCN: 机器、工人或系统的产出量。它是“被放出来的量”，不是最终形成的局面。

entries.definition: the sudden start of disease, war, or violence. It names a breaking out, not a result.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病、战争或暴力的突然爆发。它指“破壳而出”，不是结果。

entries.definition: a view or forecast. It is what you look out at, or forward to, not what came out.
entries.definitionCN: 景色；前景展望。它是你向外看、向前看的东西，不是出来的结果。

entries.definition: what happens because of something else. It is the broadest term and can name anything from a sum to a consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 因另一事物而发生的事。它是最宽泛的词，可以指从计算结果到后果的任何东西。

entries.definition: a result that follows logically or causally, often with a sense of importance or responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 按逻辑或因果随之而来的结果，常含重要性或责任意味。

entries.definition: the change produced by a cause. It stresses the change itself rather than the final situation.
entries.definitionCN: 原因造成的变化。它强调变化本身，而不是最终局面。

entries.definition: the final or eventual result of a series of events. It is informal and stresses the end of a long story.
entries.definitionCN: 一系列事件最终的结局。它较口语化，强调一个长故事的最后收束。

normalIntro.en: Five spelling hooks, then three abstract pictures of a process arriving at its end.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个拼写钩子，再用三个“过程抵达终点”的抽象画面。

normal.en: out + come: what comes out at the end.
normal.cn: out + come：最后“走出来”的那个东西。

normal.en: outcome ends in -come just as become: something becomes visible at the end.
normal.cn: outcome 和 become 一样以 -come 结尾：某物在最后变得可见。

normal.en: An election outcome is the scoreboard after the last vote is counted.
normal.cn: 选举的 outcome 就是最后一张票计完后那块记分牌。

normal.en: Learning outcomes are written before the course, like a destination on a ticket.
normal.cn: learning outcomes 写在课程之前，像车票上的目的地。

normal.en: Primary outcome is the one number a trial promises to report.
normal.cn: primary outcome 是一项试验承诺要报告的那个数字。

abstract.en: An outcome is the shape a process leaves behind after it stops moving.
abstract.cn: 结果是过程停止运动后留下的那个形状。

abstract.en: You can design an outcome without being able to control it: the end is a target, not a guarantee.
abstract.cn: 你可以设计一个结果，却无法控制它：终点是目标，不是保证。

abstract.en: Every decision sends something out into the world, and that something comes back as the room you live in.
abstract.cn: 每个决定都往世界里送出某样东西，而那样东西会作为你居住的房间返回。

examples.en: No one could predict the outcome of the talks.
examples.cn: 没有人能预测会谈的结果。

examples.en: The study measured three outcomes: pain, mobility, and sleep quality.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了三个结局指标：疼痛、活动能力与睡眠质量。

examples.en: A good process does not always produce a good outcome.
examples.cn: 好的过程并不总能产生好的结果。

dict_mnemonic.note: 记成“从过程里走出来（out）并到达（come）的东西”。
dict_mnemonic.text: out（向外）+ come（来）→ 出来的结果 → 结果、结局

root: 英语本族复合词：out（向外、进入视野）+ come（来）；1788 年见于苏格兰英语，无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: The senses go from any result, to consequences and contest results, then to measured endpoints in medicine, education, law, and statistics.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从任何“结果”出发，走到后果与比赛结果，再到医学、教育、法律与统计中可测量的终点。

core.en: A path reaching its end, where a mark is left behind
core.cn: 一条路走到尽头，在那里留下一个印记

branches.en: General result: what an event or process finally produced.
branches.cn: 一般结果：一个事件或过程最终产生的东西。

branches.en: Formal endings: the result of a contest, or of a legal case.
branches.cn: 正式终点：比赛的结果，或案件的结果。

branches.en: Measured endings: a patient's health result, or a study's primary endpoint.
branches.cn: 可测量的终点：患者的健康结果，或研究的主要终点。

branches.en: Ends declared in advance: a hoped-for result, or a learning outcome.
branches.cn: 事先声明的终点：期望的结果，或学习成果。

branches.en: Consequence: the word looks back at what a decision cost.
branches.cn: 后果：这个词回看一个决定付出了什么代价。

intro.en: Outcome belongs to the huge out- family and the even larger come family. Both halves are native English, so there is no Latin root here.
intro.cn: outcome 属于庞大的 out- 词族，也属于更大的 come 词族。两半都是英语本族词，因此这里没有拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: out is Old English ut, from Proto-Germanic *ut-, and come is Old English cuman, from Proto-Germanic *kwem-.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：out 是古英语 ut，来自原始日耳曼语 *ut-；come 是古英语 cuman，来自原始日耳曼语 *kwem-。

items.meaning: that which comes out of a process
items.example: The outcome was better than expected.
The outcoming of the vote was delayed.
items.exampleCN: 投票结果的公布被推迟了。

items.meaning: to move toward and arrive at a point

items.example: Her income doubled after the promotion.
items.exampleCN: 升职后她的收入翻了一倍。

items.meaning: to get over an obstacle and win through
items.example: They overcame the shortage of funds.

items.meaning: about to come; willing to give information
items.meaningCN: 即将到来的；乐于提供信息的
items.example: The forthcoming report will cover the trial.
items.exampleCN: 即将发布的报告将涵盖这项试验。

items.meaning: an arrival; the approach of something
items.example: The coming of winter changed the plan.
items.exampleCN: 冬天的到来改变了计划。

items.meaning: to come to be; to grow into
a variable used to judge a result in research
items.example: Pain score was the main outcome measure.
items.exampleCN: 疼痛评分是主要的结局测量指标。

definition_zh: 户外的；室外的；露天的；户外用的
definition_en: happening, used or placed in the open air rather than inside a building
core_image: 学校后山草地上搭起的简易舞台，两旁的树当了幕布，观众就坐在草地上
scene: 春天一到，学校后山那片草地就成了舞台，孩子们把桌椅搬出去，在树荫下排节目。The school holds an outdoor concert on the grass every spring.
sceneCN: 这里 outdoor 是「户外的」（第 1 个义项：在建筑物之外举行）；句意为学校每年春天在草地上办一场户外音乐会，画面是后山草地上的简易舞台与坐着的观众。

pos.zh: 户外的；室外的；露天的；户外用的

derivatives.zh: 由 outdoor 去掉形容词用法、加副词词尾 -s 构成，义为「在露天；在户外」
由 outdoors 加形容词词尾 -y 构成，义为「喜欢户外活动的」
把 outdoor 的 out 换成 in 构成的同构反义词，义为「室内的」

senses.title: Happening in the open air
senses.definition: taking place outside a building rather than under a roof
senses.definitionCN: 在建筑物之外、而不是在屋顶之下举行
senses.example: The wedding was an outdoor ceremony in the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 那场婚礼是在花园里举行的户外仪式。
senses.why: The compound is out plus door, so whatever is outdoor happens beyond the doorway; the threshold is the line the word keeps pointing at.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词是 out 加 door，所以户外的事情都发生在门之外；门槛就是这个词一直指着的那条线，义项直接落在「门外」的空间上。

senses.title: Open to the sky, without a roof
senses.definition: describing a place or structure that has no roof and is open to the weather
senses.definitionCN: 形容场所或构筑物没有屋顶，直接对着天气敞开
senses.example: They ate at a long outdoor table beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河边一张露天长桌旁吃饭。
senses.why: A place beyond the door with nothing over it is exposed to sun and rain, so the word can describe the shelter as well as the event.
senses.whyCN: 一个在门之外、头顶又空无一物的场所，就直接暴露在日晒雨淋之下，所以这个词既能说活动，也能说场所本身；露天义强调「没有遮蔽」这一层。

senses.title: Made for use outside
senses.definition: designed to be used in the open air, as clothes, furniture or equipment
senses.definitionCN: 专为在露天使用而设计，如衣物、家具或器材
senses.example: She bought a pair of outdoor shoes for the mountain trip.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这次登山买了一双户外鞋。
senses.why: Once the word marks the open air, makers label whatever is built to endure that weather, and the adjective shifts from place to purpose.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词标出了露天场所，制造商就把为那种天气而造的东西也标上它，形容词便从「地点」转向「用途」；户外装备义由此而来。

intro.en: Outdoor is a compound of two Old English words, out and door, shortened from the older phrase out of doors in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: outdoor 是两个古英语词 out 与 door 的复合，十八世纪从较早的短语 out of doors 缩略而来。

items.en: The reconstructed forms ut and dur- gave both halves their Germanic shape, so the compound was built entirely inside English's own word family.
items.cn: 重构形式 ut 与 dur- 给了两半各自的日耳曼形态，整个复合词都建在英语自身的词族之内。

items.en: Out came from the adverb ut, and door from duru, the word for an opening that can be shut.
items.cn: out 出自副词 ut，door 出自名词 duru，后者指可以关上的一个开口。

items.en: Middle English already said out of doors for being in the open air, a phrase that kept door as the boundary of the house.
items.cn: 中古英语已经用 out of doors 表示「在露天」，这个短语仍把门当作屋子的边界。

items.en: The three-word phrase was shortened into the single attributive adjective outdoor, which then stood before nouns like life and games.
items.cn: 这个三词短语缩成了一个作定语的形容词 outdoor，随后站到 life、games 这类名词前面。

items.en: Modern English keeps outdoor for the adjective, outdoors for the adverb, and pairs the word with indoor on the other side of the wall.
items.cn: 现代英语把 outdoor 留给形容词、outdoors 留给副词，并让这个词与墙另一侧的 indoor 成对使用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the compound's own family and its mirror opposite; the near-meaning group gathers words for air, outside space and open dining.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词自己的词族与镜像反义词；近义组收表示露天、外部空间与户外用餐的词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in the open air.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「在露天」的副词。

entries.definition: Existing or used inside a building.
entries.definitionCN: 在建筑物内存在或使用的。

entries.definition: Fond of activities in the open air.
entries.definitionCN: 喜欢户外活动的。

entries.definition: The older phrase from which outdoor was shortened.
entries.definitionCN: outdoor 由之缩略而成的较早短语。

entries.definition: Happening or existing outside, with no roof above.
entries.definitionCN: 在室外发生或存在、上方没有屋顶的。

entries.definition: Not inside a building, or the external part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 不在建筑物之内，或某物的外部。

entries.definition: In the open air, especially of eating.
entries.definitionCN: 在露天，尤指用餐。

entries.definition: The outer surface or side of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的外表面或外侧。

normalIntro.en: The word is a doorway turned into an adjective, so its hooks return to the door, the open sky beyond it, and the things made to survive out there.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把一道门口变成形容词，记忆钩子都回到那扇门、门外的天空，以及为在门外存活而做的东西。

normal.en: Outdoor is simply out plus door, so the word points at everything on the other side of a doorway.
normal.cn: outdoor 就是 out 加 door，所以这个词指着门口另一侧的一切。

normal.en: The older phrase out of doors did the same work in three words before English shortened it into one adjective.
normal.cn: 较早的 out of doors 用三个词做同样的事，后来英语把它压成一个形容词。

normal.en: Outdoors is the adverb and outdoor the adjective, and that final s is the only difference between them.
normal.cn: outdoors 是副词，outdoor 是形容词，两者的差别只在末尾那个 s。

normal.en: Indoor is the mirror image built the same way with in, so the pair marks the two sides of one wall.
normal.cn: indoor 是用 in 按同样办法造出的镜像，这一对词标出同一道墙的两侧。

normal.en: Outdoor furniture and outdoor clothes are named for the weather they must endure, not for the place alone.
normal.cn: outdoor furniture 与 outdoor clothes 是按它们必须承受的天气命名，而不只是按地点命名。

abstract.en: A stage set on grass with trees standing in for curtains is the word at its clearest.
abstract.cn: 草地上搭起的舞台、拿树当幕布，就是这个词最清楚的样子。

abstract.en: A doorway with sun on one side and shadow on the other is the line the word draws.
abstract.cn: 一道门，一侧有阳光、一侧有阴影，就是这个词划出的界线。

abstract.en: A pair of boots left by a tent shows the adjective following a person out of the house.
abstract.cn: 帐篷旁放着的一双靴子，显示这个形容词跟着人走出了屋子。

examples.en: The school holds an outdoor concert on the grass every spring.
examples.cn: 学校每年春天在草地上办一场户外音乐会。

examples.en: They ate at a long outdoor table beside the river.
examples.cn: 他们在河边一张露天长桌旁吃饭。

examples.en: She bought a pair of outdoor shoes for the mountain trip.
examples.cn: 她为这次登山买了一双户外鞋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特多」——奥在门外，多是门；门外的这片天，就是户外。

root: outdoor 由古英语 ut（在外）与 duru（门）合成，十八世纪从短语 out of doors 缩略为形容词；两半都属日耳曼语词族，没有拉丁同源词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the far side of a door; the senses move from an event held there, to a place with no roof, to the gear made to be used out there.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是门的另一侧；义项从在那一侧举行的活动，转到没有屋顶的场所，再转到为在那一侧使用而造的装备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough stage on a grassy slope behind the school, trees standing in for curtains, the audience seated on the grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：学校后山坡草地上的简易舞台，树充当幕布，观众坐在草地上。

branches.en: a wedding standing on a garden lawn
branches.cn: 站在花园草坪上的婚礼

branches.en: a long table beside a river with no roof above
branches.cn: 河边上方无顶的长桌

branches.en: boots by a tent, made for wet ground
branches.cn: 帐篷旁为湿地而做的靴子

branches.en: one open space, used once for a ceremony and once for a meal
branches.cn: 同一片露天空地，一次用于仪式，一次用于吃饭

branches.en: clothing chosen for weather rather than for walls
branches.cn: 按天气而非按墙壁挑选的衣物

intro.en: The word joins an Old English adverb for outside with the Old English noun for door, then grows an adverb, an adjective and a mirror opposite from the same pattern.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语中表示「在外」的副词与表示「门」的名词连在一起，再按同一模式长出副词、形容词与镜像反义词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 在户外；在露天；户外；露天场所；野外；大自然
definition_en: in or into the open air, outside a building; also the open air itself, especially when thought of as a place to live, work or play
core_image: 帐篷门帘被拉开，人一步跨出去，头顶突然空出一大片
scene: 清晨的营地，帐篷门帘被拉开，有人端着一杯热水走到草地上，抬头看没有屋顶的天空。She prefers to sleep outdoors whenever the weather allows.
sceneCN: 这里是「在户外、在露天」（第 1 个义项：在建筑物外面）；句意为只要天气允许，她更愿意睡在露天。图中可辨识物件：帐篷门帘、草地、热水杯。

pos.zh: 在户外；在露天
户外；露天场所；野外；大自然

derivatives.zh: 由 out 与 door 复合、再加 -s 构成副词；outdoor 是它的形容词形式，义为「户外的；露天的」
由 outdoors 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「喜爱户外活动的；适合户外的」
由旧短语 out of doors 连写而成，义为「在户外」，是 outdoors 的另一种写法

senses.title: Outside a building, in the open air
senses.definition: in or into the open air, on the far side of a door or wall rather than inside a building
senses.definitionCN: 在或进入建筑物之外的露天环境，也就是在门或墙的另一侧，而不是在屋里
senses.example: The children played outdoors until the light faded.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在户外玩到天光暗下来。
senses.why: The word is a compressed phrase: out of doors once meant literally passing through the door to the space beyond it, so the adverb still carries a step from inside to outside.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是短语压缩来的：out of doors 原意是「走出门去、到门外的空间」，所以这个副词到今天还带着从室内跨到室外的那一步。

senses.title: The open air as a place to be
senses.definition: the open air, thought of as a place where people spend time, work or rest, as in the outdoors
senses.definitionCN: 把露天的空气当作一个可以待着、干活或休息的地方，如 the outdoors
senses.example: After a week at a desk, he needed the outdoors.
senses.exampleCN: 在桌前坐了一周之后，他需要到户外去。
senses.why: Once the adverb had named the space beyond the door, English could put the definite article in front of it and treat that space as a place with a name, which is how the noun appeared.
senses.whyCN: 副词先给门外那片空间起了名，英语再在它前面加上定冠词，把那片空间当成一个有名字的地方，名词用法就是这样长出来的。

senses.title: Wild open country
senses.definition: open country with woods, hills or water, far from buildings, especially as a place for recreation
senses.definitionCN: 远离建筑的田野、树林、山岭或水域，尤指供人游玩休憩的开阔地带
senses.example: They spent the holiday exploring the great outdoors.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这个假期用来探索广阔的大自然。
senses.why: The phrase the great outdoors added great to the same noun and pushed the meaning from any open air toward wide, unbuilt land, where the absence of roofs becomes the whole attraction.
senses.whyCN: the great outdoors 在同一个名词前加了 great，把意思从「任何露天的空气」推向开阔、没有建筑的土地；在那里，屋顶的缺席本身成了全部吸引力。

intro.en: Outdoors began as the phrase out of doors, a plain description of going through a door into the open, and the modern spelling fuses those words into one adverb and noun.
intro.cn: outdoors 起初是短语 out of doors，平平常常地描述「出了门到露天去」，现代拼写把这几个词粘成了一个副词和一个名词。

items.en: Old English had duru for a door and ūt for out, the two plain words that the later phrase would join.
items.cn: 古英语用 duru 表示门、用 ūt 表示向外，这两个平常的词后来被拼进同一个短语。

items.en: Middle English said out of dores, literally out of the doors, for leaving a house for the open air.
items.cn: 中古英语说 out of dores，字面就是「出了那些门」，用来表示离开屋子到露天去。

items.en: Writers began to set the phrase down as one word, outdoors, and to use it as an adverb of place.
items.cn: 到了十六、十七世纪，作者们把这个短语写成一个词 outdoors，用作表示地点的副词。

items.en: The fused form took a definite article and became a noun, the outdoors, naming the open air as a place rather than a direction.
items.cn: 这个合成形式带上定冠词，成了名词 the outdoors，把露天的空气当作一个地方来指，而不是一个方向。

items.en: Modern English adds the fixed phrase the great outdoors and uses the word for camping, sport and open-air work.
items.cn: 现代英语又添出固定说法 the great outdoors，并用这个词谈露营、运动和露天工作。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the door word and the forms built on the same compound; the near-meaning group collects other names for the air and land outside buildings.
note.cn: 形近组收表示门的词以及由同一复合结构长出的形式；近义组收其他表示「建筑物之外的空气与土地」的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective form, placed before a noun for things done or used in the open air.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，放在名词前，指在露天进行或使用的事物。

entries.definition: Fond of outdoor activities and comfortable in the open air.
entries.definitionCN: 喜爱户外活动、在露天也自在的。

entries.definition: The older phrase from which the single word was formed, meaning outside a house.
entries.definitionCN: 合成词所由来的旧短语，意为在屋子外面。

entries.definition: Used for things inside a building, the reverse of outdoor.
entries.definitionCN: 指建筑物内部的事物，与 outdoor 相对。

entries.definition: The space outside buildings, with no roof above it.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物之外、头顶没有遮蔽的空间；露天。

entries.definition: Land away from towns, with fields, woods and small villages.
entries.definitionCN: 远离城镇、有田野树林与村庄的土地；乡下。

entries.definition: The physical world of plants, animals, weather and landscape.
entries.definitionCN: 植物、动物、天气与地貌构成的物质世界；大自然。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic compound of out and door, so the mnemonics keep the picture of stepping through a doorway into open air.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 out 与 door 的日耳曼语复合，所以联想都围绕「穿过一道门、走进露天」的画面。

normal.en: Outdoors is out of doors compressed, and the door is still visible inside the modern spelling.
normal.cn: outdoors 是 out of doors 压缩来的，那扇门在现代拼写里仍看得见。

normal.en: The plural doors is a fossil of the older phrase out of dores, kept even after the words fused.
normal.cn: 复数 doors 是旧短语 out of dores 留下的化石，词粘成一个以后它也没消失。

normal.en: Outdoor is the adjective; outdoors is the adverb and the noun.
normal.cn: outdoor 是形容词，outdoors 是副词兼名词。

normal.en: Outdoorsy adds -y and describes a person who likes being in the open air.
normal.cn: outdoorsy 加 -y，形容喜欢待在露天的人。

normal.en: The great outdoors uses the definite article to turn open air into a named place.
normal.cn: the great outdoors 用定冠词，把露天的空气变成一个有名字的地方。

abstract.en: A hand pushing a door open and a foot landing on grass.
abstract.cn: 一只手推开门，一只脚落在草上。

abstract.en: The word keeps a door inside it, which is why the open air still feels like something you pass through.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一扇门留在里面，所以露天总像是你必须穿过什么才到得了。

abstract.en: A roof is what the word leaves behind, and that absence is the whole point.
abstract.cn: 屋顶是这个单词留在身后的东西，而这份缺席正是它的全部意思。

examples.en: The children played outdoors until the light faded.
examples.cn: 孩子们在户外玩到天光暗下来。

examples.en: After a week at a desk, he needed the outdoors.
examples.cn: 在桌前坐了一周之后，他需要到户外去。

examples.en: They spent the holiday exploring the great outdoors.
examples.cn: 他们把这个假期用来探索广阔的大自然。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凹特道兹」——走到门外那片地上，头顶一下就空了；记住 outdoors 是户外。

root: outdoors 是英语短语 out of doors 的合写形式：out（向外）源自古英语 ūt，doors 是 door（古英语 duru）的复数，原意「出了门、到门外」。材料属日耳曼语，拉丁语没有可靠的同族派生词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the space on the far side of a door; the adverb names being there, and the noun names the place itself, first any open air and then wide wild country.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「门另一侧的那片空间」；副词说的是人在那里，名词说的是那个地方本身，先是任何露天，再是开阔的野外。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tent flap pulled open onto grass under an empty sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：帐篷门帘被拉开，外面是草地和没有屋顶的天空。

branches.en: a person walking out of a lit room into a dark garden
branches.cn: 一个人从亮着的房间走进昏暗的花园

branches.en: children running across grass until dusk
branches.cn: 孩子们在草地上跑到天黑

branches.en: a camper sitting alone in the open with a cup in hand
branches.cn: 露营的人端着杯子独自坐在露天

branches.en: a ridge line seen from a trail far from any town
branches.cn: 从远离城镇的小路上望见山脊

branches.en: a map marking a wide park with no buildings
branches.cn: 一张标出没有建筑的大片公园的地图

intro.en: The word is a Germanic compound of out and door, with a plural ending left over from the old phrase.
intro.cn: 这个词是 out 与 door 的日耳曼语复合词，还带着旧短语遗留下来的复数词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for the door element.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，其中表示门的那个成分没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

the plural of door, kept inside the compound
items.meaningCN: door 的复数，被保留在合成词里

done or used in the open air
plural marker left from the old phrase

definition_zh: 外面的；外部的；外围的；远离中心的；表面的
definition_en: on or near the outside of something; farther from the centre than another part; and also describing what is shown rather than felt inside
core_image: 两只叠在一起的碗，手先摸到最外那一圈，凉得更快
scene: 冬天的早上，两只叠着的碗放在窗台上，手碰到最外面那一圈，凉得更快。The outer layer of paint had begun to peel.
sceneCN: 这里是「外面的、外部的」（第 1 个义项：最靠外的一层）；句意为最外面那层漆已经开始脱落。图中可辨识物件：叠着的碗、窗台、剥落的漆面。

pos.zh: 外面的；外部的；外围的；远离中心的；表面的

derivatives.zh: 由 outer 加最高级后缀 -most 构成，义为「最外面的；离中心最远的」
由 outer 与 wear 复合而成，义为「外衣；外套类服装」
由 out 加方向后缀 -ward 构成，义为「向外的；外表的」，与 outer 侧重位置不同

senses.title: On the outside of something
senses.definition: on or near the outside of a thing, especially of a layer that covers or surrounds something else
senses.definitionCN: 在一件东西的外面或靠近外面，尤指覆盖、包围另一物的那一层
senses.example: A thin outer shell protects the seed.
senses.exampleCN: 一层薄薄的外壳保护着种子。
senses.why: Outer is the comparative of out, so it marks the side that is more out than the other, which is why it usually names the covering layer when two layers are compared.
senses.whyCN: outer 是 out 的比较级，标出两者中「更靠外」的那一边，所以当两层东西相比时，它通常指起覆盖作用的那一层。

senses.title: Farther from the centre
senses.definition: situated at a greater distance from the centre, as in the outer ring of a city or the outer planets
senses.definitionCN: 离中心更远的位置，如城市的外环或外侧的行星
senses.example: They moved from the crowded centre to an outer suburb.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从拥挤的市中心搬到一处外围郊区。
senses.why: Because the comparative points away from a middle, the word also measures distance from a centre, so a city or a solar system can be split into inner and outer zones.
senses.whyCN: 既然比较级指的是背离中心的方向，这个词也用来量离中心的距离，于是一座城市或一个星系都能分成内圈与外圈。

senses.title: Shown rather than felt
senses.definition: belonging to the surface of a person or thing, as opposed to what is hidden or felt inside
senses.definitionCN: 属于人或物的表层，与藏在里面、真实感到的东西相对
senses.example: Beneath his outer calm, he was badly shaken.
senses.exampleCN: 他表面镇定，内心却受到很大震动。
senses.why: If outer names the layer people can see, then a person's composure can be spoken of as an outer layer, with the hidden feeling lying behind it.
senses.whyCN: 如果 outer 指的正是别人看得见的那一层，那么一个人的镇定也可以说成一层外皮，藏起来的情绪就在它后面。

intro.en: Outer is an English comparative of out, formed by adding -er to the adverb; it is generally taken to have replaced an older comparative that survives in utter.
intro.cn: outer 是英语用副词 out 加 -er 构成的比较级；一般认为它取代了一个更老的比较级，那个形式留在 utter 里。

items.en: The reconstructed root behind out meant outward, and it supplied the adverb in several Germanic languages.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ūt 意为向外，在几种日耳曼语里都提供了这个副词。

items.en: Old English ūt meant out, and its comparative ūtera named what is more out or farther out; that form survives in utter.
items.cn: 古英语 ūt 意为在外、向外，它的比较级 ūtera 指更靠外的东西；这个形式后来留在 utter 里。

items.en: Middle English added -er to out again and produced outer, generally read as a newer doublet of the older comparative.
items.cn: 中古英语又给 out 加了一次 -er，造出 outer，一般认为它是那个更老比较级的新替身。

items.en: English fixed outer as the adjective for the outside member of a pair or set, especially in outer wall, outer ring and outer room.
items.cn: 英语把 outer 固定为形容词，指一对或一组事物里靠外的那一个，尤其用于外墙、外环、外间。

items.en: Modern English extends it to space and cities, giving outer space, outer suburbs and the superlative outermost.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到太空与城市，产生 outer space、outer suburbs 以及最高级 outermost。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the out family and its older comparative; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for what lies on or beyond a surface.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 out 词族及其更老比较级展开；近义组收表示「位于表面或表面之外」的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb and preposition from which outer was formed by adding a comparative ending.
entries.definitionCN: outer 由它加比较级词尾构成，意为向外、在外。

entries.definition: Farthest out, or farthest from the centre.
entries.definitionCN: 最外面的；离中心最远的。

entries.definition: An older comparative of out, now mainly meaning complete or absolute.
entries.definitionCN: out 更老的比较级，现在主要表示「完全的、彻底的」。

entries.definition: Going or pointing away from the inside.
entries.definitionCN: 向外去的；朝外的。

entries.definition: Coming from or belonging to the outside.
entries.definitionCN: 来自或属于外部的。

entries.definition: The outside surface of a building or object.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物或物体的外表面。

entries.definition: On the edge or outer boundary of something.
entries.definitionCN: 在边缘或外围的。

entries.definition: The flat top or outside layer of a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 物体的表层或外表面。

normalIntro.en: Outer is a comparative of out, so the mnemonics compare two positions and always pick the one farther from the middle.
normalIntro.cn: outer 是 out 的比较级，所以联想始终在比较两个位置，并且总挑离中间更远的那个。

normal.en: Outer is out plus the comparative ending -er, so it literally says more out.
normal.cn: outer 是 out 加比较级词尾 -er，字面就是「更靠外」。

normal.en: Old English had a comparative ūtera, and that older form survives in utter.
normal.cn: 古英语本来就有比较级 ūtera，这个更老的形式留在 utter 里。

normal.en: Outermost adds -most and pushes the comparison to the extreme.
normal.cn: outermost 加 -most，把比较推到最尽头。

normal.en: Outerwear is outer plus wear: the clothing worn as the outside layer.
normal.cn: outerwear 是 outer 加 wear：当作最外层穿的衣服。

normal.en: Outward uses -ward, which marks direction, while outer marks position.
normal.cn: outward 用 -ward 标方向，而 outer 标位置。

abstract.en: Two bowls stacked, and the hand reaching for the cooler rim.
abstract.cn: 两只碗叠着，手先摸到更凉的那一圈外沿。

abstract.en: A city drawn as two rings: the word only makes sense when there is a middle to be far from.
abstract.cn: 把城市画成两个圈：这个词只有在存在一个可供远离的中心时才成立。

abstract.en: A calm face with something behind it: the outside layer is also a screen.
abstract.cn: 一张平静的脸背后藏着东西：外层同时也是一道屏风。

examples.en: A thin outer shell protects the seed.
examples.cn: 一层薄薄的外壳保护着种子。

examples.en: They moved from the crowded centre to an outer suburb.
examples.cn: 他们从拥挤的市中心搬到一处外围郊区。

examples.en: Beneath his outer calm, he was badly shaken.
examples.cn: 他表面镇定，内心却受到很大震动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凹特」——两只碗叠着，手总先摸到外面那一圈；记住 outer 是外面的。

root: outer 由古英语副词 ūt（向外）加比较级后缀 -er 构成，一般认为它是更老的比较级 ūtera（今存于 utter）的替身；属日耳曼语材料，拉丁语没有可靠的同族派生词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a comparison of two positions; the senses go from the covering layer, to distance from a centre, to the face a person shows.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「两个位置的比较」；义项从覆盖的那一层，到离中心的距离，再到一个人露出的表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two stacked bowls, the outer rim wider and cooler to the touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只叠在一起的碗，外沿更宽，摸上去也更凉。

branches.en: a hand testing the cooler rim of a bowl
branches.cn: 一只手试探碗沿更凉的那一圈

branches.en: paint flaking from the outer wall of a house
branches.cn: 房屋外墙剥落的漆

branches.en: a ring road drawn around a crowded centre
branches.cn: 拥挤市中心外围画出的环线

branches.en: a telescope pointed at the outer planets
branches.cn: 望远镜对准外侧的行星

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: a place or pipe through which something flows out; a socket that supplies electricity; a shop or channel through which goods are sold; and a way of releasing energy or feelings
core_image: 墙根下一个半圆的排水口，水从那里流出去，汇进外面的沟
scene: 雨后的墙角积了一小片水，水沿着砖缝往低处走，最后钻进墙根那个半圆的口子。Water poured from the outlet into the gutter.
sceneCN: 这里是「出口、排放口」（第 1 个义项：让水或气体流出去的口子）；句意为水从那个排水口流进沟里。图中可辨识物件：墙角积水、砖缝、半圆形排水口。

pos.zh: 出口；排放口；插座；电源接口；销路；经销店；发泄途径

senses.title: An opening through which something flows out
senses.definition: an opening, pipe or channel through which water, air or another substance leaves a container, building or machine
senses.definitionCN: 让水、空气或其他物质离开容器、建筑物或机器的口子、管道或通道
senses.example: Water poured from the outlet into the gutter.
senses.exampleCN: 水从排水口流进沟里。
senses.why: Outlet is out plus let, literally a letting out: the word names the point where something is allowed to go, so its first sense is a physical opening.
senses.whyCN: outlet 是 out 加 let，字面就是「放出去」：这个词指某样东西被允许离开的那个点，所以最初的意思是一个实体的口子。

senses.title: A socket that supplies electricity
senses.definition: a socket in a wall or on a device where a plug is connected to the electricity supply
senses.definitionCN: 墙上或设备上供插头接入电源的插座
senses.example: The lamp would not work until she found another outlet.
senses.exampleCN: 她找到另一个插座，台灯才亮起来。
senses.why: Electricity is imagined as a flow, so the point where current leaves the wiring for a device borrowed the word already used for a water opening.
senses.whyCN: 电被想象成一种流，于是电流离开线路、进入电器的那一点，就借用了原本给水口子的那个词。

senses.title: A shop or channel that sells goods
senses.definition: a shop, company or channel through which goods are sold, especially one selling a manufacturer's products
senses.definitionCN: 把货物卖出去的店铺、公司或渠道，尤指销售某厂商产品的店
senses.example: The brand opened a new outlet on the edge of town.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌在城镇边缘开了一家新的经销店。
senses.why: Goods also need a way out of the warehouse, so the market where a product leaves the maker's hands took the same name, and later the shop itself was called an outlet.
senses.whyCN: 货物同样需要一条走出仓库的路，于是产品离开厂家、进入市场的那一环沿用了同一个词，后来那家店本身也被叫作 outlet。

senses.title: A way of releasing pent-up energy
senses.definition: a means of expressing or releasing strong feelings, energy or creativity that might otherwise be held in
senses.definitionCN: 把压抑的情感、精力或创造力表达、释放出去的途径
senses.example: Running became his outlet after the long working days.
senses.exampleCN: 在漫长的工作日之后，跑步成了他的发泄途径。
senses.why: When pressure has no physical opening, English extends the same image to feelings: an outlet is wherever the built-up force is finally allowed to escape.
senses.whyCN: 当压力找不到实体的口子，英语就把同一个画面挪到情绪上：凡是积起来的力量最终得以泄出的地方，都叫 outlet。

intro.en: Outlet is an English compound of out and let, where let still carries its old sense of allowing something to go; the word first named a way out for water and air.
intro.cn: outlet 是 out 与 let 的英语复合词，其中 let 仍保留「让某物走」的旧义；这个词最初指水与空气的出路。

items.en: The verb lǣtan meant to let or allow, and it supplied the second half of the compound.
items.cn: 动词 lǣtan 意为让、允许，提供了这个复合词的后半部分。

items.en: Middle English joined out and let for a place where something is let out, chiefly water or air.
items.cn: 中古英语把 out 与 let 合起来，指某物被放出去的地方，主要是水或空气。

items.en: The word was used for the mouth of a river, a drain, or any passage by which a liquid escapes.
items.cn: 这个词用来指河口、排水沟，或任何让液体流走的通道。

items.en: A further sense named the market where goods find a way out, and American usage applied the word to the socket that lets current out of a wall.
items.cn: 后来又有一义，指货物找到出路的市场；美式用法又把这个词用在让电流离开墙壁的插座上。

items.en: Modern English speaks of retail outlets, media outlets and an outlet for anger, all keeping the idea of something escaping.
items.cn: 现代英语说 retail outlets、media outlets 以及 an outlet for anger，都保留着「有东西流出去」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the let family and the parallel compounds built with out; the near-meaning group collects words for openings, supply points and markets.
note.cn: 形近组收 let 词族以及用 out 平行造出的复合词；近义组收表示「口子、供电点与市场」的词。

entries.definitionCN: 让东西进入的口子，与 outlet 相对；入口、进水口。

entries.definition: The place where a drain or river discharges its water.
entries.definitionCN: 排水沟或河流把水排出去的地方。

entries.definition: To allow something to happen or to go.

entries.definition: The flow of something out of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 某物从一处流出的过程或流量。

entries.definition: A hollow or contact point into which something is plugged.
entries.definitionCN: 供插接的凹口或接触点；插座。

entries.definition: A way out of a building or a road.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物或道路的出入口；出口。

entries.definition: A place or system where goods are bought and sold.
entries.definitionCN: 买卖货物的场所或体系；市场。

entries.definition: An opening that lets air or gas escape.
entries.definitionCN: 让空气或气体逸出的口子；通风口。

normalIntro.en: Outlet pairs a Germanic out with the verb let, so every sense keeps the picture of something being allowed to leave.
normalIntro.cn: outlet 把日耳曼语的 out 与动词 let 配在一起，所以每个义项都保留「有东西被放出去」的画面。

normal.en: Outlet is out plus let, so the first picture is something being let out.
normal.cn: outlet 是 out 加 let，所以第一个画面是有东西被放出去。

normal.en: Let here is the old verb for allow, not the rented-room sense of the modern noun.
normal.cn: 这里的 let 是表示「允许」的旧动词，不是现代名词里「出租房」的意思。

normal.en: Inlet uses in instead of out and reverses the direction.
normal.cn: inlet 把 out 换成 in，方向就反了过来。

normal.en: An electrical outlet lets current out of the wiring into a device.
normal.cn: 电源插座让电流从线路里流出来，进入电器。

normal.en: Retail outlet and outlet store keep the commercial sense of goods finding a way out.
normal.cn: retail outlet 与 outlet store 保留了货物找到出路的那层商业含义。

abstract.en: A half-round drain at the foot of a wall, water slipping through it.
abstract.cn: 墙根一个半圆的排水口，水从那里溜出去。

abstract.en: The same hole serves water, current, goods and anger, because all four are things that must go somewhere.
abstract.cn: 同一个口子同时应付水、电流、货物和怒气，因为四者都是必须有个去处的东西。

abstract.en: A blocked outlet turns a drain into a pool, which is what happens when a feeling has nowhere to go.
abstract.cn: 出口一堵，排水沟就变成一摊水；情绪无处可去时也是如此。

definition_en: the line that marks the outer edge of a shape; a short account of the main points of something; and the verbs for drawing that edge or for summarizing those points
core_image: 铅笔沿着影子的边缘走了一圈，纸上只剩一条线
scene: 夜里灯从侧面照过来，墙上落下一个人的影子，孩子拿铅笔沿着影子的边慢慢描。He drew the outline of his hand on the paper.
sceneCN: 这里是「轮廓、外形」（第 1 个义项：描出物体外缘的那条线）；句意为他在纸上描出自己手的轮廓。图中可辨识物件：侧照的灯、墙上的影子、铅笔。

pos.zh: 轮廓；外形；概要；提纲
勾画轮廓；概述；略述

senses.title: The line marking the outer edge
senses.definition: the line that marks the outer edge of a shape or object, especially as seen against a background
senses.definitionCN: 标出一个形状或物体外缘的线，尤指在背景衬托下看到的
senses.example: He drew the outline of his hand on the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他在纸上描出自己手的轮廓。
senses.why: Out plus line gives a line that travels around the outside of a thing, so the noun begins as the visible boundary of a shape rather than anything inside it.
senses.whyCN: out 加 line 就是「沿外面走的那条线」，所以这个名词最初指一个形状看得见的外缘，而不是它内部的东西。

senses.title: A summary of the main points
senses.definition: a short description or plan that gives the main points of something without the supporting details
senses.definitionCN: 只给要点、不含细节的简短说明或方案
senses.example: She wrote an outline before starting the essay.
senses.exampleCN: 她动笔写文章之前先列了提纲。
senses.why: If a line can mark the edge of a shape, a line of argument can mark the edge of a subject, so the word came to mean the bare frame of a text or a plan.
senses.whyCN: 既然一条线可以标出一个形状的边，一串论点也可以标出一个题目的边，于是这个词转而指文章或方案最简的骨架。

senses.title: To draw the outer edge of something
senses.definition: to draw or trace the outer edge of a shape, usually with a single continuous line
senses.definitionCN: 用线条描出一个形状的外缘，通常只画一条连续的线
senses.example: The map outlines the coast in fine black ink.
senses.exampleCN: 地图用细细的黑线勾出海岸的轮廓。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb without changing its picture: to outline is to make the very line the noun names, so the action and its result share one image.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词时画面没变：to outline 就是画出名词所指的那条线，于是动作和结果共用同一个图像。

senses.title: To describe something in general terms
senses.definition: to give the main points of a plan, idea or argument without going into detail
senses.definitionCN: 只讲计划、想法或论述的要点，不深入细节
senses.example: The manager outlined the changes at the morning meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 经理在晨会上概述了这些变动。
senses.why: From drawing the edge of a shape, the verb moves to marking the edge of a subject, which is exactly what a summary does: it traces the boundary and leaves the interior blank.
senses.whyCN: 从描出一个形状的边，这个动词转到标出一个题目的边，而概括做的正是这件事：把边界走一遍，把里面留空。

intro.en: Outline is an English compound of out and line, and line itself goes back through French to Latin linea, a thread of linen used for measuring.
intro.cn: outline 是 out 与 line 的英语复合词，而 line 本身经法语可追到拉丁语 linea，指用来量长短的亚麻线。

items.en: Linea meant a line, a string or a linen thread, and it is the source of the English word line.
items.cn: linea 意为线、绳或亚麻线，是英语 line 的来源。

items.en: Old French ligne carried the Latin word into English with the sense of a drawn line or a boundary.
items.cn: 古法语 ligne 把拉丁词带进英语，意思是一条画出的线或一条边界。

items.en: English joined out and line to name the boundary line of a figure, seen against the space around it.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语把 out 与 line 合起来，指图形与周围空间相接的那条边界线。

items.en: The same noun was applied to a sketch containing only contours and then to a summary of the main points of a text.
items.cn: 同一个名词先被用于只含轮廓的草图，随后又指文章要点的摘要。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb, and uses outline in course outlines, project outlines and the phrase in outline.
items.cn: 现代英语又添出动词用法，并把 outline 用在课程大纲、项目提纲以及 in outline 这个说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the out compound and the line family; the near-meaning group collects words for shapes seen from outside and for short summaries.
note.cn: 形近组收 out 复合词与 line 词族；近义组收表示「从外面看到的形状」以及简短摘要的词。

normal.en: Outline is out plus line: a line drawn around the outside.

normal.en: A course outline does the same job as a drawn edge: it shows where the subject begins and ends.
normal.cn: 课程大纲做的事和描边一样：它让你看出这门课从哪里开始、到哪里结束。

abstract.en: A line that shows the edge but leaves the middle empty is also a good way to summarize a long argument.
abstract.cn: 一条只走边、中间留空的线，也正好是概括长篇论述的好办法。

abstract.en: Every outline is a promise that the empty space inside will be filled later.
abstract.cn: 每条轮廓都暗含着承诺：里面的空白以后会填上。
